# Cohere: A Profile of its LLMs and Enterprise AI Strategy

October 3, 2025  
Updated August 4, 2026  
20 min read

Learn about AI company Cohere, its enterprise focus, Command family of LLMs, North agent platform, and path to a potential 2026 IPO. Updated with $240M ARR, Tiny Aya models, and latest developments.

IntuitionLabs Report

*Updated August 4, 2026.*

Cohere Inc. is a Canadian-American AI company specializing in [large language models (LLMs)](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/chatgpt-understanding-architecture-llm) and enterprise AI solutions. Founded in 2019 by Aidan Gomez (CEO), Nick Frosst, and Ivan Zhang – all former Google Brain researchers – Cohere was built on the same [transformer architecture](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/key-innovations-behind-chatgpt) (“Attention Is All You Need”) that underpins models like GPT-5.2 ([[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#:~:text=natural%20language%20processing%20%20tasks.,founders%20attended%20%2031.%5E%7B%5B11)) ([[2]](https://www.forbes.com/profile/aidan-gomez/#:~:text=Aidan%20Gomez%20cofounded%20Cohere%20after,5%20billion%2C%20per%20PitchBook)). The company has raised over $1.5 billion to date, backed by investors such as NVIDIA, AMD, Oracle, Salesforce, PSP Investments, and Canadian pension funds, and its valuation has rocketed from a few billion in 2023 to roughly $7 billion by late 2025 ([[3]](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/22/cohere-raises-500m-to-beat-back-generative-ai-rivals/#:~:text=The%20round%2C%20which%20also%20had,total%20raised%20to%20%24970%20million)) ([[4]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=Chadwick%20spoke%20with%20BetaKit%20at,valuation%20to%20%247%20billion%20USD)). Cohere’s company page lists locations in Toronto, New York, London, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, and Seoul ([[5]](https://cohere.com/about)). With $240 million in annual recurring revenue achieved in 2025 – surpassing its $200M target – and an IPO widely anticipated in 2026, Cohere has entered a pivotal new phase ([[6]](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/13/coheres-240m-year-sets-stage-for-ipo/)).

The company focuses on AI for enterprises rather than consumer apps. Cohere builds LLMs and tools to power secure, private, and customizable AI for large businesses and government clients. Its flagship products include a suite of language models (the **“Command”** family), developer APIs for tasks like text generation, embeddings, and reranking, and platform tools for building AI agents and search. Cohere customers – such as Oracle, LivePerson, RBC, Bell, and STC Group – use these models for applications like document summarization, chatbot automation, intelligence search, and data analysis in highly regulated sectors ([[7]](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/22/cohere-raises-500m-to-beat-back-generative-ai-rivals/#:~:text=Unlike%20OpenAI%2C%20Anthropic%2C%20Mistral%20and,like%20Oracle%2C%20LivePerson%20and%20Notion)) ([[8]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=Cohere%20sells%20its%20LLMs%20and,software%20developer%20Ensemble%20Health%20Partners)). The company emphasizes data privacy and security: its LLMs can be deployed on any cloud or even [on-premises](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/enterprise-ai-code-assistants-air-gapped-environments), “bringing the model to your data” rather than the other way around ([[9]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-command-r-a-powerful-llm-optimized-for-enterprise-ai#:~:text=search%20and%20retrieval%20models%20now,within%20their%20preferred%20cloud%20environment)) ([[10]](https://cohere.com/products#:~:text=,insights%20grounded%20in%20your%20data)).

01

## History and Milestones

Cohere was founded in Toronto in 2019. Its company page identifies Aidan Gomez as co-founder and CEO, with Nick Frosst and Ivan Zhang as co-founders, and describes the company’s focus as enterprise AI ([[5]](https://cohere.com/about)).

In June 2022, Cohere relaunched the independent For.ai research community as **Cohere For AI**, a dedicated research lab and community. Cohere renamed the initiative **Cohere Labs** in April 2025. ([[11]](https://cohere.com/research)) (Hooker oversaw this lab until departing Cohere in summer 2025 ([[12]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=One%20immediate%20challenge%20for%20Pineau,skyrocketing%20demand%20for%20AI%20talent)).)

On the product side, Cohere made its platform publicly available on November 15, 2021, offering developers access to text-generation, embedding, and classification models ([[13]](https://cohere.com/blog/the-cohere-platform-is-now-publicly-available-2)). In December 2022, it released a multilingual text-understanding model for semantic search within and across languages ([[14]](https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/multilingual-text-understanding-model-language-detection)). Throughout 2023 and 2024, Cohere iteratively improved its model lineup: introducing *co.chat()* and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) features in late 2023, and rolling out new versions like **Command R+** (April 2024) which offer longer context windows (128K tokens) and advanced capabilities ([[15]](https://www.bigdatawire.com/this-just-in/cohere-introduces-command-r-a-scalable-llm-built-for-business/#:~:text=,to%20automate%20sophisticated%20business%20processes)) ([[16]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-command-r-a-powerful-llm-optimized-for-enterprise-ai#:~:text=Command%20R%2B%20is%20optimized%20for,to%20data%20privacy%20and%20security)).

In parallel, Cohere forged strategic partnerships: in June 2023, Oracle announced a partnership with Cohere to provide generative AI services for businesses ([[17]](https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/oracle-generative-ai-2023-06-13/)). Separately, a March 2024 report said Oracle NetSuite planned to add more than 200 AI features, including generative-AI capabilities ([[18]](https://www.axios.com/2024/03/28/oracle-netsuite-generative-ai)). In mid-2023, Cohere teamed up with McKinsey to integrate [generative AI](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/symbolic-ai-vs-generative-ai-wolfram-chatgpt) into client workflows, and with LivePerson to provide custom LLMs for customer service solutions ([[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#:~:text=generative%20AI%20services%20to%20help,2)). By mid-2024, its models were available on [Microsoft Azure](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/secure-chatgpt-azure-integration), continuing its "cloud-agnostic" approach ([[20]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-command-r-a-powerful-llm-optimized-for-enterprise-ai#:~:text=Cohere%20remains%20independent%20and%20cloud,within%20their%20preferred%20cloud%20environment)).

The pace of innovation accelerated through late 2025 and into 2026. In January 2025, Cohere officially launched **North**, its AI agent workspace platform, in early access ([[21]](https://siliconangle.com/2025/01/09/cohere-introduces-llm-powered-north-productivity-platform/)). In August 2025, Cohere released **Command A Translate**, a specialized 111B-parameter translation model supporting 23 languages with state-of-the-art quality ([[22]](https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/2025-08-28-command-a-translate)). On January 28, 2026, Cohere launched **Model Vault**, a private platform for securely serving and scaling Cohere models ([[23]](https://cohere.com/blog/model-vault)). In December 2025, Cohere unveiled **Rerank 4**, with *pro* and *fast* variants for multilingual reranking. Cohere describes the models as supporting 32,768-token contexts and 100+ languages; it does not describe them as self-learning ([[24]](https://cohere.com/models-overview)). In February 2026, Cohere Labs released the **Tiny Aya** family – open-weight multilingual models with 3.35 billion parameters supporting 70+ languages that can run on laptops and edge devices without internet connectivity ([[25]](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/17/cohere-launches-a-family-of-open-multilingual-models/)).

02

## Leadership and Key Personnel

Cohere’s leadership combines AI researchers and seasoned executives. CEO **Aidan Gomez** co-founded the company in 2019; he is best known for co-authoring the original transformer paper at age 20 ([[26]](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/22/cohere-raises-500m-to-beat-back-generative-ai-rivals/#:~:text=Aiden%20Gomez%20launched%20Cohere%20in,and%20Stability%20AI%E2%80%99s%20%208)) ([[2]](https://www.forbes.com/profile/aidan-gomez/#:~:text=Aidan%20Gomez%20cofounded%20Cohere%20after,5%20billion%2C%20per%20PitchBook)). Co-founders **Ivan Zhang** and **Nick Frosst** remain in senior roles. **Martin Kon**, a former CFO of YouTube (Google), joined Cohere in early 2023 as President & COO; he oversaw business operations and fundraising through multiple rounds ([[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#:~:text=Gomez%20is%20the%20company%27s%20CEO.,12)) ([[28]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=Kon%20will%20keep%20his%20seat,Gartner%2C%20Cohere%E2%80%99s%20head%20of%20communications)). In August 2025, after raising a new $500M round, Cohere announced Kon would step down from day-to-day duties (remaining as a board member and senior advisor) ([[29]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=TORONTO%20%E2%80%94%20Cohere%20president%20Martin,financing%2C%20The%20Logic%20has%20learned)) ([[30]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=Talking%20Points)).

Cohere’s research and product teams have seen high-profile changes in 2025. Sara Hooker, who led Cohere Labs (the nonprofit research arm), announced her exit in August 2025 ([[12]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=One%20immediate%20challenge%20for%20Pineau,skyrocketing%20demand%20for%20AI%20talent)). She is being succeeded in spirit by **Joëlle Pineau**, a veteran AI researcher and professor from McGill University. Pineau had been VP of AI Research at Meta (overseeing projects like the open **Llama** models) and left Meta in May 2025; in August 2025 she was hired as Cohere’s **Chief AI Officer** ([[31]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=Now%2C%20the%20company%20is%20bringing,research%2C%20product%2C%20and%20policy%20teams)). Pineau’s role is to guide Cohere’s research strategy, model development, and recruitment of top talent ([[31]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=Now%2C%20the%20company%20is%20bringing,research%2C%20product%2C%20and%20policy%20teams)) ([[32]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=Pineau%20said%20she%E2%80%99s%20particularly%20interested,other%20in%20the%20real%20world)). Cohere also promoted **Phil Blunsom** (a prominent NLP researcher, formerly Google and DeepMind) to CTO in mid-2025, replacing Saurabh Baji who departed ([[33]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=Cohere%20has%20also%20appointed%20a,sales%20in%20Korea%20and%20Japan)). A new CFO, **François Chadwick** (ex-KPMG partner and former Uber acting CFO), joined concurrently in August 2025 ([[33]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=Cohere%20has%20also%20appointed%20a,sales%20in%20Korea%20and%20Japan)) ([[34]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=Chadwick%2C%20who%20previously%20served%20as,%E2%80%9D)).

Other key figures include **Jaron Waldman** (Chief Product Officer since 2022) and co-founders Zhang and Frosst leading technology teams. The company’s board and investors also play active roles; for example, Democratizing AI advocates like Inovia Ventures (lead investor) and PSP Investments have been vocal supporters. As of 2025, Cohere’s senior team remains a mix of North American and European talent, reflecting its global ambitions.

03

## Core Products and Model Families

Cohere’s product suite centers on AI models and tools “built for business,” often under the **“Cohere” brand**. Its core offerings are:

* **Command (LLM) family:** High-performance generative models for text tasks. Key variants include *Command A+* (released in May 2026), *Command A*, *Command A Vision*, *Command A Translate*, and *Command R7B*; earlier Command R and Command R+ models also remain part of the family ([[35]](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-plus)). These models support very long context windows (up to 128K or 256K tokens) and are optimized for enterprise scenarios like document understanding, question-answering, summarization, code assistance, and multi-step “tool use” automation. In April 2024 Cohere released **Command R+**, a 104-billion-parameter model with 128K context, optimized for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), multi-lingual support (10 major languages), and integration with external tools/APIs ([[15]](https://www.bigdatawire.com/this-just-in/cohere-introduces-command-r-a-scalable-llm-built-for-business/#:~:text=,to%20automate%20sophisticated%20business%20processes)) ([[16]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-command-r-a-powerful-llm-optimized-for-enterprise-ai#:~:text=Command%20R%2B%20is%20optimized%20for,to%20data%20privacy%20and%20security)). Command R+ was touted as “the most performant” model Cohere had built and was said to outperform similar offerings on RAG and tool use benchmarks ([[16]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-command-r-a-powerful-llm-optimized-for-enterprise-ai#:~:text=Command%20R%2B%20is%20optimized%20for,to%20data%20privacy%20and%20security)) ([[36]](https://www.bigdatawire.com/this-just-in/cohere-introduces-command-r-a-scalable-llm-built-for-business/#:~:text=Our%20latest%20model%20builds%20on,security%20that%20we%E2%80%99re%20known%20for)). In mid-2025, Cohere unveiled **Command A** (111B parameters, 256K context) and **Command A Vision** (a multimodal variant that ingests images) ([[37]](https://docs.cohere.com/llms.txt#:~:text=,Details%20and)) ([[38]](https://docs.cohere.com/llms.txt#:~:text=Model%5D%28https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.cohere.com%2Fchangelog%2F2025,Vision%2C%20Cohere%27s%20first%20model%20able)). Cohere describes Command R7B (7B parameters) as the smallest, fastest model in the R series, ideal for latency-sensitive chatbots and scaling to many users ([[39]](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-r7b#:~:text=Command%20R7B%20is%20the%20smallest,unlocks%20dramatically%20cheaper%20deployment%20infrastructure%E2%80%94such)).
* **Command A Translate:** Released August 2025, this specialized 111B-parameter translation model achieves state-of-the-art performance across 23 languages including English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi ([[22]](https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/2025-08-28-command-a-translate)). It represents Cohere's first dedicated machine translation offering, targeting enterprises needing high-quality multilingual content workflows.
* **Embed models:** Transformers that convert text (and now multimodal content) into semantic vectors for retrieval/search. Cohere's latest **Embed v4** is a multimodal embedding model supporting both text and image inputs, including interleaved text-and-image content for document understanding and visual search. It supports Matryoshka Embeddings (dimensions of 256, 512, 1024, and 1536) and well over 100 languages ([[40]](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/models)). These vector models, along with **Cohere Rerank 4**, support retrieval-augmented workflows. Cohere documents *rerank-v4.0-pro* as a multilingual option for quality and complex use cases, and *rerank-v4.0-fast* as a multilingual option for lower-latency, higher-throughput use cases; the documentation does not specify self-learning behavior ([[41]](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/rerank)). Embeddings and reranking are available through API endpoints for indexing and searching corpora.
* **North (AI Agent Platform):** Officially launched in early access in January 2025, North is Cohere's flagship AI agent/workspace solution for enterprises ([[21]](https://siliconangle.com/2025/01/09/cohere-introduces-llm-powered-north-productivity-platform/)). It combines LLMs, search, and AI agents in a single secure platform, letting organizations build custom agents for HR, finance, customer support, IT, and other business functions. North draws on Cohere's models and an organization's own data to automate workflows such as summarizing reports, drafting emails, conducting research across multilingual repositories, and performing complex multi-step tasks ([[42]](https://cohere.com/products#:~:text=An%20enterprise,for%20immediate%20impact)) ([[43]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=Cohere%E2%80%99s%20main%20product%20is%20a,computers%20rather%20than%20remote%20servers)). North can be deployed in a VPC or on-premises for maximum security. Notably, Royal Bank of Canada has partnered with Cohere to develop **North for Banking**, a specialized version designed for financial institutions – one of the first major enterprise deployments of the platform ([[44]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-north-to-redefine-enterprise-ai-with-security-and-customization-at-its-core)).
* **Compass (Enterprise Search):** Compass is an end-to-end search system that Cohere says can process images, presentations, spreadsheets, and documents across languages. Cohere describes it as using retrieval models including Embed and Rerank, with deployment options in a VPC, on premises, or in Model Vault; the company does not publish sufficient methodology on this page to substantiate a general task-time-reduction figure ([[45]](https://cohere.com/compass)).
* **Model Vault:** Launched on January 28, 2026, Model Vault is Cohere’s private platform for securely serving and scaling Cohere models ([[23]](https://cohere.com/blog/model-vault)).
* **Tiny Aya (Open Multilingual Models):** Released in February 2026 by Cohere Labs, the Tiny Aya family consists of open-weight 3.35B-parameter models supporting 70 languages and designed for local deployment. The family comprises the pretrained *Tiny Aya Base*, the broadly balanced *Tiny Aya Global*, and regional instruction-tuned variants: *Tiny Aya Earth* for West Asian and African languages, *Tiny Aya Fire* for South Asian languages, and *Tiny Aya Water* for European and Asia-Pacific languages. The instruction-tuned variants are available through the Cohere API, and the models are available through Hugging Face ([[46]](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/tiny-aya)).

In addition to these, Cohere maintains developer-facing API endpoints such as `/v2/chat`, `/v2/embed`, and `/v2/rerank`; the legacy `/v1/classify` endpoint is deprecated ([[47]](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/deprecations)). For example, Cohere’s models run on Google Cloud (TPUs/GCP) and are also available through **Microsoft Azure AI** (via a strategic partnership announced 2024) ([[48]](https://www.bigdatawire.com/this-just-in/cohere-introduces-command-r-a-scalable-llm-built-for-business/#:~:text=As%20we%20continue%20to%20serve,to%20accelerate%20enterprise%20AI%20adoption)). The company offers both on-demand API access and dedicated clusters for large enterprise deployments ([[49]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=officer,promoting%20Phil%20Blunsom%20to%20CTO)). Overall, Cohere positions its product line as a “full-stack AI” for businesses: from frontier LLMs to workspace tools, all under strong security and customization controls ([[50]](https://cohere.com/products#:~:text=Get%20to%20value%20faster%20with,from%20day%20one%20of%20deployment)) ([[51]](https://cohere.com/products#:~:text=Security)).

04

## Model Capabilities and Performance

Cohere publishes model-specific evaluations, which should be treated as vendor-reported results rather than independent cross-vendor rankings. For Command A+, released on May 20, 2026, Cohere reports results from public benchmarks and internal North evaluations; it says the internal evaluations use an LLM-as-a-judge method ([[35]](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-plus); [Introducing Command A+](https://cohere.com/blog/command-a-plus)).

Command R7B’s current dated release, `command-r7b-12-2024`, has a 128K-token context window. Cohere characterizes it as a small, fast model for RAG, tool use, agents, and related multi-step tasks, but the available documentation does not establish a configuration-controlled latency comparison with GPT-3.5 or another provider’s model ([[52]](https://docs.cohere.com/v1/docs/models)).

TechCrunch reported in mid-2025 that Cohere’s models had fallen behind the state of the art on raw benchmarks, while noting the company’s enterprise focus on security and deployment ([[53]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=But%20Cohere%E2%80%99s%20AI%20models%20have,hasn%E2%80%99t%20scaled%20like%20its%20competitors)). Cohere’s enterprise positioning emphasizes deployment, integration, and retrieval-augmented workflows; this positioning should not be read as an independently established comparison of model capability or cost. CFO François Chadwick explains this as a conscious strategy: Cohere invests heavily in training power but “doesn’t carry [its] customers’ full compute cost,” delivering high performance at lower price to users ([[54]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=According%20to%20Francois%20Chadwick%2C%20Cohere,capitalized%2C%20and%20foundational%20AI%20field)).

Cohere publishes model-specific capability, context-window, and deployment information, but a general conclusion about comparative quality, throughput, latency, or cost would require a reproducible benchmark with disclosed model versions, endpoints, workload, hardware, region, and measurement method. The sources cited here do not provide that basis.

05

## Business Model, Recent Funding, and Growth

Cohere primarily offers enterprise AI models, APIs, and workplace software rather than a consumer chatbot product. Its public materials describe products for business teams, including enterprise agents, retrieval, and private deployment ([[5]](https://cohere.com/about)) ([[55]](https://cohere.com/north)). Cohere's growth trajectory has been striking: from roughly $35 million in annualized revenue in early 2025 to **$240 million in ARR** by year-end 2025, surpassing its $200M target and achieving over 50% quarter-over-quarter growth throughout the year ([[6]](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/13/coheres-240m-year-sets-stage-for-ipo/)) ([[56]](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/13/ai-startup-cohere-revenue-ipo.html)). Gross margins averaged around 70% in 2025. This growth is fueled by new enterprise contracts, the launch of North/Compass, and significant government deals. CEO Aidan Gomez stated publicly in October 2025 that an IPO is coming "soon," and with the hire of IPO-experienced CFO François Chadwick, a **2026 IPO** is widely anticipated by analysts and investors ([[57]](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/coheres-multilingual-sovereign-ai-moat-ahead-of-a-2026-ipo/)).

Cohere has raised multiple rounds, with total funding exceeding $1.5 billion. Major milestones include a $270 M Series C in mid-2023, a $500 M round in July 2024 (valuing the company at ~$5.5 B) ([[3]](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/22/cohere-raises-500m-to-beat-back-generative-ai-rivals/#:~:text=The%20round%2C%20which%20also%20had,total%20raised%20to%20%24970%20million)), another $500 M in August 2025 at a $6.8 B post-money valuation ([[58]](https://cohere.com/blog/august-2025-funding-round)) ([[59]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=For%20Cohere%20this%20is%20a,pipeline%2C%20and%20recruiting%20top%20talent)), and a $100 M second close in September 2025 (with participation from the Business Development Bank of Canada and Nexxus Capital), lifting the valuation to ~$7 B ([[60]](https://cohere.com/blog/september-2025-funding-round)) ([[4]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=Chadwick%20spoke%20with%20BetaKit%20at,valuation%20to%20%247%20billion%20USD)). Notably, Cohere’s investors encompass a mix of venture firms (Radical Ventures, Inovia) and strategic corporates (Oracle, Salesforce, AMD, NVIDIA) ([[61]](https://thelogic.co/news/exclusive/cohere-martin-kon-president-depature/#:~:text=Cohere%E2%80%99s%20investors%20include%20major%20Canadian,tech%20firms%20Oracle%20and%20Salesforce)). Under the Canadian Sovereign AI Compute Strategy, the Government of Canada finalized an investment of up to **$240 million** in Cohere’s $725 million domestic-compute project in March 2025. The government identified Cohere as the first recipient of its AI Compute Challenge. ([[62]](https://www.canada.ca/en/innovation-science-economic-development/news/2025/03/government-of-canada-finalizes-investment-to-support-canadian-born-ai-leader-cohere.html))

This robust financing has allowed Cohere to expand headcount dramatically – from roughly 250 employees in mid-2024 to over 800 by early 2026 – and invest in global sales. Cohere’s public company page lists locations in Seoul, London, and Paris, alongside its North American locations ([[5]](https://cohere.com/about)). Canada's AI Minister and Industry Minister have publicly lauded Cohere as a "national champion," highlighting Cohere's role in Canada's AI strategy ([[63]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=On%20stage%20at%20ALL%20IN%2C,greater%20appetite%20from%20Canadian%20buyers)). Cohere's partnerships and revenue growth put it in the same league as other enterprise-AI startups; however, as CFO Chadwick noted, its valuation/revenue multiple (~30×) remains lower than that of peer startups (e.g. OpenAI, Perplexity, Anthropic) on a relative basis ([[64]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=Cohere%20is%20on%20track%20to,Anthropic%2C%20according%20to%20some%20estimates)). The company told investors it anticipates another year of "rapid growth" in 2026.

06

## Competition and Industry Positioning

In the crowded AI landscape, Cohere competes with both “Labs” (open research groups) and corporate AI vendors. Its main direct competitors are the other large-model companies: OpenAI, partnered with and backed by Microsoft; Anthropic (backed by Google & AWS); Mistral AI; Google DeepMind (Gemini); Meta’s research labs; and emerging players like AI21 Labs or Chinese firms. Cohere differentiates itself in several ways:

* **Enterprise focus:** Unlike OpenAI or Anthropic, which spawned consumer-facing products (ChatGPT, Claude) or aim for general AGI, Cohere is **laser-focused on enterprise needs** ([[65]](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/14/cohere-hires-long-time-meta-research-head-joelle-pineau-as-its-chief-ai-officer/#:~:text=But%20while%20its%20rivals%20are,agencies%2C%20emphasizing%20privacy%20and%20security)). It customizes models for industry workflows, provides dedicated support, and prioritizes security/compliance ([[7]](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/22/cohere-raises-500m-to-beat-back-generative-ai-rivals/#:~:text=Unlike%20OpenAI%2C%20Anthropic%2C%20Mistral%20and,like%20Oracle%2C%20LivePerson%20and%20Notion)) ([[9]](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-command-r-a-powerful-llm-optimized-for-enterprise-ai#:~:text=search%20and%20retrieval%20models%20now,within%20their%20preferred%20cloud%20environment)). This is a conscious strategy: new CFO Chadwick emphasizes that Cohere “spends money on compute” for training but ensures customers pay less to deploy, giving an ROI-focused value proposition ([[54]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=According%20to%20Francois%20Chadwick%2C%20Cohere,capitalized%2C%20and%20foundational%20AI%20field)). Cohere’s platform allows clients to continue using their existing cloud and AI tools while adding Cohere’s capabilities, thereby “carving out a niche” in a well-funded market ([[54]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=According%20to%20Francois%20Chadwick%2C%20Cohere,capitalized%2C%20and%20foundational%20AI%20field)) ([[43]](https://betakit.com/in-a-field-dominated-by-ai-giants-cohere-makes-its-case/#:~:text=Cohere%E2%80%99s%20main%20product%20is%20a,computers%20rather%20than%20remote%20servers)).
* **Privacy and deployment:** Cohere invests in secure deployment options. Its models can run in private cloud or air-gapped environments, appealing to banks, governments, and healthcare. **Cohere Inc.** is a Canadian multinational technology company focused on [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence"). Cohere specializes in [large language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_models "Large language models") and AI products for regulated industries, particularly the finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and energy fields, as well as the public sector. Cohere was founded in 2019 by [Aidan Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aidan_Gomez "Aidan Gomez"), Ivan Zhang, and [Nick Frosst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Frosst "Nick Frosst") and is headquartered in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), with offices in [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal "Montreal"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), and [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"). In April 2026, Cohere agreed to acquire German AI firm [Aleph Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleph_Alpha "Aleph Alpha").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 2017, a team of researchers at [Google Brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Brain "Google Brain") introduced the [transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)") machine learning architecture in "[Attention Is All You Need](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_Is_All_You_Need "Attention Is All You Need")", which demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on a variety of [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing") tasks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-nvidia-8) In 2019, Aidan Gomez, one of its co-authors, along with Nick Frosst,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-Silcoff-2021-9) another researcher at Google Brain, founded Cohere with Ivan Zhang, with whom Gomez had done research at FOR.ai.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-rival-11) All of the co-founders attended the [University of Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Toronto "University of Toronto").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-12)

Gomez is the company's CEO.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-rival-11) In December 2022, Martin Kon, the former CFO of [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), became president and COO.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-rising-13)

In November 2021, [Google Cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Cloud_Platform "Google Cloud Platform") announced they would help power Cohere's platform using their infrastructure, and Cloud's [TPUs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensor_Processing_Unit "Tensor Processing Unit") would be used by Cohere for the development and deployment of their products.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-nlp-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-seriesa-15)

In June 2022, Cohere launched **Cohere Labs** (previously called Cohere For AI), a nonprofit research lab and community to contributing open-source, fundamental machine learning research. It was led by [Sara Hooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Hooker "Sara Hooker"), a former research scientist at Google Brain[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-16) until her departure in September 2025. Cohere Labs is now led by Marzieh Fadaee.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-17)

In December 2022, Cohere released a multilingual model for understanding text that would work with over 100 languages, to help users search for documents by meaning instead of keywords. This type of process was not previously widely available in languages other than English.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-rising-13)

On September 12, 2023, it was announced that Cohere had become one of fifteen tech companies to sign on to a voluntary [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") commitment on measures for testing, reporting, and research on the risks of AI.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-18) On September 27, 2023, it was announced that Cohere had also signed Canada's voluntary code of conduct for AI, to promote the responsible development and management of advanced generative AI systems.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-19)

In 2024, Cohere opened an office in New York City.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-headquarters22-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-22) In 2025, they expanded to Montreal, Canada,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-23) Paris,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-24) and Seoul.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-26)

In May 2025, Cohere acquired Ottogrid, a Vancouver-based platform that develops enterprise tools for automating certain kinds of market research.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-27) In June 2025, it was announced that Cohere had partnered with the governments of Canada and the United Kingdom to expand the use of AI in the public sector.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-28) In August 2025, Cohere hired [Joelle Pineau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joelle_Pineau "Joelle Pineau") as Chief A.I. Officer and Francois Chadwick, a former [Uber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uber "Uber") executive and [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG") US partner, as its first Chief Financial Officer.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-29)

On April 10, 2026, Cohere and [Aleph Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleph_Alpha "Aleph Alpha") announced that they were in talks to merge, with the potential deal having the support of the German government.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-30) On April 24, Cohere and Aleph Alpha announced that Cohere would acquire Aleph Alpha. While the terms of the deal were not publicly disclosed, an anonymous individual told _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Times "New York Times")_ it would make the combined companies worth $20 billion. The deal was made in a bid to challenge AI dominance from primarily the United States as well as China, with the _New York Times_ noting that they had struggled to keep up in attracting investment from US-based companies. The terms of the deal also involve $600 million in investment to Cohere from [Schwarz Gruppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwarz_Gruppe "Schwarz Gruppe"), already prominent investors in Aleph Alpha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-31)

In September 2026, Cohere and [Aleph Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleph_Alpha "Aleph Alpha") signed a definitive merger agreement. The combined company will operate under the name _Cohere_, with headquarters in Toronto and Berlin, while Aleph Alpha's Heidelberg office will focus on research. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-32)

## Products

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Products")]

Considered an alternative to [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI"),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-oracle-33) Cohere works on generative AI, building technology that businesses can use to deploy chatbots, search engines, copywriting, summarization, and other AI-driven products.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-nvidia-8)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-34) Cohere specializes in [large language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model "Large language model"): AI trained to digest text from internal data or publicly available sources to understand how to process and respond to prompts with increasing sophistication.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-rising-13)

The Cohere platform is available through an [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API "API") as a managed service and through platforms such as [Amazon SageMaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_SageMaker "Amazon SageMaker") and Google's Vertex AI. It is cloud agnostic and not tied to a particular cloud service.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-rival-11) Cohere's generative AI technology is embedded into several [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Corporation "Oracle Corporation") products, and its chat capabilities are embedded into [Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce "Salesforce") products.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-oracle-33)

In March 2025, Cohere's nonprofit research lab introduced Aya Vision, an AI model that can describe images, translate text, and summarize information. The model is free for research but is not permitted to be used for commercial purposes.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-35)

## Partnerships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Partnerships")]

On June 13, 2023, [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Corporation "Oracle Corporation") announced a partnership with Cohere to provide [generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") services to help organizations automate end-to-end business processes. Cohere's technology is integrated into Oracle Fusion Cloud, Oracle NetSuite, and Oracle industry-specific applications.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-36)[McKinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKinsey_&_Company "McKinsey & Company") announced a collaboration with Cohere, to help organizations integrate generative AI into their operations on July 18, 2023.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-37) Cohere also partnered with software company [LivePerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LivePerson "LivePerson") to offer customized large language models for businesses in 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-nvidia-8)

In 2024, Cohere partnered with [Fujitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujitsu "Fujitsu") in co-developing Takane, a Japanese LLM.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-39)

In January 2025, in partnership with [RBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Bank_of_Canada "Royal Bank of Canada"), Cohere introduced North for Banking, a secure generative AI platform in financial services.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-40) A partnership with [LG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG "LG") developed a Korean LLM and customized the North platform for Korean companies.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-41)

In May 2025, Cohere partnered with SAP to integrate its AI models into SAP's Business Suite and make them available through SAP AI Core's generative AI hub.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-42) In November 2025, Cohere's North platform was among the AI offerings integrated into the launch of SAP's European AI Cloud.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-43)

Cohere announced a collaboration with Dell Technologies, making Dell the first infrastructure provider to offer Cohere North, the company's secure AI workspace platform.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-45) Cohere also entered the healthcare sector through a partnership with Ensemble Health Partners, a revenue cycle management company, to deploy agentic AI solutions for healthcare providers' administrative workflows.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-47)

In July 2025, Cohere announced a partnership with [Bell Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_Canada "Bell Canada") to provide AI services to government and enterprise customers. Bell Canada will deploy Cohere's technology on its data centre infrastructure and offer AI solutions to clients. Bell also implemented Cohere's North platform for internal operations.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-48)

In December 2025, [Thales Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Group "Thales Group") and Cohere partnered to apply AI systems in naval and maritime defence operations.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-50)

[Hanwha Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanwha_Ocean "Hanwha Ocean") contracted with Cohere in January 2026 to integrate its generative AI technologies in ship design and procurement processes.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-53)

In March 2026, [Saab AB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saab_AB "Saab AB") announced a partnership with Cohere that utilizes the latter's AI technologies to support the [GlobalEye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GlobalEye "GlobalEye") surveillance aircraft.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-55)

As of April 2026, Cohere provides generative AI solutions for the [Aston Martin F1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Martin_in_Formula_One "Aston Martin in Formula One"). Cohere's technologies are applied in the teams' engineering, performance assessments, and operations.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-57)

## Funding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Funding")]

On September 7, 2021, Cohere announced they had raised $40 million in Series A funding led by [Index Ventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Index_Ventures "Index Ventures"); Index Ventures partner [Mike Volpi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Volpi "Mike Volpi") also joined Cohere's board.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-nlp-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-seriesa-15) The round also included Radical Ventures, [Section 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section_32_(company) "Section 32 (company)"), and AI-experts [Geoffrey Hinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton "Geoffrey Hinton"), [Fei-Fei Li](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fei-Fei_Li "Fei-Fei Li"), [Pieter Abbeel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieter_Abbeel "Pieter Abbeel"), and [Raquel Urtasun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raquel_Urtasun "Raquel Urtasun").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-Silcoff-2021-9)

In February 2022, Cohere announced they had raised $125 million in series B funding led by [Tiger Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Global_Management "Tiger Global Management").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-58) In June 2023, Cohere raised an additional $270 million in series C funding from investors including Inovia Capital, [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Corporation "Oracle Corporation"), [Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce "Salesforce"), and [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), at a valuation of $2.2 billion.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-nvidia-8)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-59)

In March 2024, it was reported that Cohere had an annualized revenue run rate of $22 million and in July 2024 it was reported they received $500 million in funding from investors including [Cisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco "Cisco"), [AMD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMD "AMD") and [Fujitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujitsu "Fujitsu") at a valuation of $5.5 billion.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-61)

In December 2024, Cohere received $240 million in public funding from the Canadian government as part of the Canadian Sovereign AI Compute Strategy to support the construction of a domestic AI [data center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-62)

As of May 2025, Cohere's annual revenue was reported to be $100 million.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-64) In October 2025, Cohere's annualized revenue reached $150 million.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-65) In February 2026, CNBC reported Cohere's revenue as $240 million.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-66)

In 2025, Cohere raised US$500 million in a funding round led by Radical Ventures and Inovia Capital, for a valuation of US$6.8 billion.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-67) Inovia's [Patrick Pichette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Pichette "Patrick Pichette") was appointed to Cohere's Board of Directors.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-68)

In September 2025, Cohere announced a second funding round, raising an additional $100 million and increasing its valuation to approximately $7 billion. The new investors included [the Business Development Bank of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_Development_Bank_of_Canada "Business Development Bank of Canada") and Nexxus Capital Management.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-70)

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Awards")]

Cohere was listed on the [Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes") AI 50 list in 2022,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-71) 2023,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-72) 2024,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-73) and 2025.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-74)

_[Fortune magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune\_(magazine) "Fortune (magazine)")_ listed the company on their 50 AI innovators list in 2023.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-75)

Cohere was listed on [CNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNBC "CNBC")'s Disruptor list in 2023[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-76) and 2024.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-77)

## Litigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Litigation")]

In February 2025, a consortium of 14 publishing companies including [The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic"), [Condé Nast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cond%C3%A9_Nast "Condé Nast"), and [Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes") sued Cohere for copyright infringement, accusing Cohere of using their content for training without permission, as well as displaying considerable portions or entire articles of their content without permission.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohere#cite_note-78)

## References

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cohere&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: References")]

["Cohere raises US$500-million, hires former Meta AI expert Joelle Pineau"](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-cohere-fundraising-former-meta-executive-joelle-pineau-ai/). _The Globe and Mail_. [Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20250815095349/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-cohere-fundraising-former-meta-executive-joelle-pineau-ai/) from the original on August 15, 2025. About

# Where enterprise AI meets real-world purpose

Cohere builds foundational models and AI solutions that help teams turn everyday effort into extraordinary impact.

Our Mission

##### We believe AI’s highest purpose is to enhance human wellbeing. We’re committed to realizing that potential by empowering businesses to scale innovation, boost productivity, and drive progress that reaches everyone.

![Image 28: Image for Aesthetics Purposes](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/rjtqmwfu/web3-prod/fc9d89a21a12957acd79906436fba5d7be89322c-1513x1619.png?auto=format&fit=max&q=80&w=1513)

Our story

### From Toronto startup to enterprise AI

2019

#### Foundations

Cohere was founded in 2019 in Toronto with a bold vision: to do whatever it takes to scale intelligence to serve humanity.

Since then, we’ve remained focused on building enterprise AI that enhances human judgment, accelerates execution, and extends what individuals and teams can achieve on their own.

![Image 30: Featured Image](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/rjtqmwfu/web3-prod/4fe9ec3304c8f3c156c96da3e70874d94d23d566-1244x991.png?auto=format&fit=max&q=80&w=1244)

![Image 31: Featured Image](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/rjtqmwfu/web3-prod/4fe9ec3304c8f3c156c96da3e70874d94d23d566-1244x991.png?auto=format&fit=max&q=80&w=1244)

2021 – 2024

#### Early growth

Between 2021 and 2024, we secured four major funding rounds (Series A through D), raising nearly $1 billion.

This support has enabled us to scale our teams, expand globally, and continually develop cutting-edge models that power practical AI applications for the world’s leading enterprises.

![Image 32](https://cohere.com/pause.svg)

![Image 33](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/rjtqmwfu/web3-prod/2d42f2ca71196197ecae94c8f2027fd55d08a6b7-611x271.gif?auto=format&fit=max&q=80&w=611)

2022

#### Research focus

In 2022, we launched Cohere Labs, our open science initiative for solving complex machine learning problems.

Today, Cohere Labs has 4,500+ community members and has published over 100 research papers.

[Learn more](https://cohere.com/research)

![Image 34: Featured Image](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/rjtqmwfu/web3-prod/bd0094095a52f522311301f99a29c627175ec599-1240x960.png?auto=format&fit=max&q=80&w=1240)

2025 – present

#### Agentic AI for the enterprise

In 2025, we launched North, our turnkey AI platform for workplace productivity.

North’s agentic capabilities and advanced retrieval allow teams to automate routine tasks, accelerate complex workflows, and surface insights securely grounded in enterprise data.

[Learn more](https://cohere.com/north)

# An Overview of Cohere's Models

Copy page

This page is for version v2 API (default). For other versions, use one of these documentation indexes: - v2 API (default): https://docs.cohere.com/v2/llms.txt - v1 API: https://docs.cohere.com/v1/llms.txt

Cohere has a variety of models that cover many different use cases. If you need more customization, you can [tune your prompts](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/crafting-effective-prompts) to adjust its behavior to your specific use case.

Cohere models are currently available on the following platforms:

*   [Cohere’s proprietary platform](https://dashboard.cohere.com/playground/chat)
*   [Amazon SageMaker](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/seller-profile?id=87af0c85-6cf9-4ed8-bee0-b40ce65167e0)
*   [Amazon Bedrock](https://us-west-2.console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/home?region=us-west-2#/providers?model=cohere.command-r-plus-v1:0)
*   [Microsoft Azure](https://ai.azure.com/explore/models/?tid=694fed05-7f6d-4ab2-8c38-9afb438eab6f&selectedCollection=cohere)
*   [Oracle GenAI Service](https://www.oracle.com/artificial-intelligence/generative-ai/generative-ai-service/)
*   [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/cohere) (see [Cohere on OpenRouter](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/cohere-on-openrouter))

At the end of each major section below, you’ll find technical details about how to call a given model on a particular platform.

## What can These Models Be Used For?

In this section, we’ll provide some high-level context on Cohere’s offerings, and what the strengths of each are.

*   The Command family of models includes [Command A+](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-plus), [Command A](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a), [Command R7B](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-r7b), [Command A Translate](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-translate), [Command A Reasoning](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-reasoning), [Command A Vision](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-vision), [Command R+](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-r-plus), [Command R](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-r), and [Command](https://cohere.com/models/command?_gl=1*15hfaqm*_ga*MTAxNTg1NTM1MS4xNjk1MjMwODQw*_ga_CRGS116RZS*MTcxNzYwMzYxMy4zNTEuMS4xNzE3NjAzNjUxLjIyLjAuMA..). Together, they are the text-generation LLMs powering tool-using agents, [retrieval augmented generation](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/retrieval-augmented-generation-rag) (RAG), translation, copywriting, and similar use cases. They work through the [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) endpoint, which can be used with or without RAG.
*   [Rerank](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/rerank) is the fastest way to inject the intelligence of a language model into an existing search system. Rerank 5, available in Pro and Fast, is our latest generation and adds Context Focus, which returns the most relevant passages within each document. It can be accessed via the [Rerank](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/rerank-1) endpoint.
*   [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/cohere-embed) improves the accuracy of search, classification, clustering, and RAG results. It powers the [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed) endpoint.
*   [Parse](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/parse) extracts structured, machine-readable data from unstructured enterprise documents, like forms and PDFs. It powers the [Parse](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/reference/parse) endpoint.
*   [Cohere Transcribe](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/transcribe) is Cohere’s dedicated audio transcription model for automatic speech recognition (ASR). It powers the [Audio Transcriptions](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/reference/create-audio-transcription) endpoint. [Cohere Transcribe Arabic](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/transcribe-arabic) is a version of the model optimized for Arabic-language audio.
*   The [Aya](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/aya) family of models are aimed at expanding the number of languages covered by generative AI. Aya Expanse covers 23 languages, and Aya Vision is fully multimodal, allowing you to pass in images and text and get a single coherent response. Both are available on the [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) endpoint.
*   The North family includes purpose-built models such as [North Small Translate](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/north-small-translate-1.0) for machine translation and [North Mini Code](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/north-mini-code-1.0) for agentic coding. Both are available through the [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) endpoint. North Mini Code also supports production deployment through [Model Vault](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/model-vault).
*   [Model Vault](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/model-vault) also runs leading third-party open models, such as DeepSeek, GLM, MiMo, Gemma, Nemotron, GPT-OSS, Phi, and Qwen, alongside Cohere’s models on dedicated infrastructure.

## Command

Command is Cohere’s default generation model that takes a user instruction (or command) and generates text following the instruction. Our Command models also have conversational capabilities, meaning they are well-suited for chat applications, and Command A Vision can interact with [image inputs](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/image-inputs).

| Model Name | Status | Description | Modality | Context Length | Maximum Output Tokens | Endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command-a-plus-05-2026` | Live | Command A+ offers the last model in the Command A family, while being Cohere’s first Mixture of Experts model, simultaneously combining vision input support, agentic, reasoning, and world-class translation capabilities into single model weights. It also can fit on 1 x B200 or 2 x H100 GPUs, while providing significant latency and throughput improvements over Command A Reasoning, making it an ideal model for any enterprise to deploy at scale. | Text, Images | 128k | 64k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-a-03-2025` | Live | Command A is our most performant model to date, excelling at tool use, agents, retrieval augmented generation (RAG), and multilingual use cases. Command A has a context length of 256K, only requires two GPUs to run, and has 150% higher throughput compared to Command R+ 08-2024. | Text | 256k | 8k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r7b-12-2024` | Live | `command-r7b-12-2024` is a small, fast update delivered in December 2024. It excels at RAG, tool use, agents, and similar tasks requiring complex reasoning and multiple steps. | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-a-translate-08-2025` | Live | Command A Translate is Cohere’s state of the art machine translation model, excelling at a variety of translation tasks on 23 languages: English, French, Spanish, Italian, German, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Russian, Polish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Dutch, Czech, Indonesian, Ukrainian, Romanian, Greek, Hindi, Hebrew, Persian. | Text | 8K | 8k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-a-reasoning-08-2025` | Live | Command A Reasoning is Cohere’s first reasoning model, able to ‘think’ before generating an output in a way that allows it to perform well in certain kinds of nuanced problem-solving and agent-based tasks in 23 languages. | Text | 256k | 32k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-a-vision-07-2025` | Live | Command A Vision is our first model capable of processing images, excelling in enterprise use cases such as analyzing charts, graphs, and diagrams, table understanding, OCR, document Q&A, and object detection. It officially supports English, Portuguese, Italian, French, German, and Spanish. | Text, Images | 128K | 8K | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r-08-2024` | Live | `command-r-08-2024` is an update of the Command R model, delivered in August 2024. Find more information in the [changelog](https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/command-gets-refreshed) | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r-plus-08-2024` | Live | `command-r-plus-08-2024` is an update of the Command R+ model, delivered in August 2024. Find more information in the [changelog](https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/command-gets-refreshed) | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r-03-2024` | Deprecated Sept 15, 2025 | Command R is an instruction-following conversational model that performs language tasks at a higher quality, more reliably, and with a longer context than previous models. It can be used for complex workflows like code generation, retrieval augmented generation (RAG), tool use, and agents. | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r-plus-04-2024` | Deprecated Sept 15, 2025 | Command R+ is an instruction-following conversational model that performs language tasks at a higher quality, more reliably, and with a longer context than previous models. It is best suited for complex RAG workflows and multi-step tool use. | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r-plus` | Deprecated Sept 15, 2025 | Alias for `command-r-plus-04-2024` | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-r` | Deprecated Sept 15, 2025 | Alias for `command-r-03-2024` | Text | 128k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command-light` | Deprecated Sept 15, 2025 | A smaller, faster version of `command`. Almost as capable, but a lot faster. | Text | 4k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `command` | Deprecated Sept 15, 2025 | An instruction-following conversational model that performs language tasks with high quality, more reliably and with a longer context than our base generative models. | Text | 4k | 4k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |

In this table, we provide some important context for using Cohere Command models on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, and more.

## North

North is Cohere’s family of purpose-built generative models. North models are available on the Cohere API for evaluation. [North Mini Code](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/north-mini-code-1.0) also supports production deployment through [Model Vault](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/model-vault).

| Model Name | Status | Description | Modality | Context Length | Maximum Output Tokens | Endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `north-small-translate-1.0` | Live | [North Small Translate](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/north-small-translate-1.0) is a 218B total / 25B active parameter MoE model purpose-built for machine translation across more than 50 languages. | Text | 16k | 16k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |
| `north-mini-code-1.0` | Live | [North Mini Code](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/north-mini-code-1.0) is a 30B total / 3B active parameter MoE model trained for agentic coding. | Text | 256k | 64k | [Chat](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat) |

### Using North Models on Different Platforms

North Mini Code is available on [OpenRouter](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/cohere-on-openrouter) under `cohere/north-mini-code:free`.

## Embed

These models can be used to generate embeddings from text or classify it based on various parameters. Embeddings can be used for estimating semantic similarity between two sentences, choosing a sentence which is most likely to follow another sentence, or categorizing user feedback. The Representation model comes with a variety of helper functions, such as for detecting the language of an input.

| Model Name | Description | Modalities | Dimensions | Context Length | Similarity Metric | Endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `embed-v5.0-pro` | Our most capable embedding model, for text and images. Higher quality than `embed-v5.0-fast`, at higher latency. | Text, Images, Mixed texts/images (i.e. PDFs) | One of ‘[256, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048 (default)]‘ | 128k | Cosine Similarity, Dot Product Similarity, Euclidean Distance | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed) |
| `embed-v5.0-fast` | A faster, lighter version of `embed-v5.0-pro`. Allows for text and images to be classified or turned into embeddings | Text, Images, Mixed texts/images (i.e. PDFs) | One of ‘[256, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048 (default)]‘ | 128k | Cosine Similarity, Dot Product Similarity, Euclidean Distance | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed) |
| `embed-v4.0` | A model that allows for text and images to be classified or turned into embeddings | Text, Images, Mixed texts/images (i.e. PDFs) | One of ‘[256, 512, 1024, 1536 (default)]‘ | 128k | Cosine Similarity, Dot Product Similarity, Euclidean Distance | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed), [Embed Jobs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed-jobs) |
| `embed-english-v3.0` | A model that allows for text to be classified or turned into embeddings. English only. | Text, Images | 1024 | 512 | Cosine Similarity | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed), [Embed Jobs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed-jobs) |
| `embed-english-light-v3.0` | A smaller, faster version of `embed-english-v3.0`. Almost as capable, but a lot faster. English only. | Text, Images | 384 | 512 | Cosine Similarity | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed), [Embed Jobs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed-jobs) |
| `embed-multilingual-v3.0` | Provides multilingual classification and embedding support. [See supported languages here.](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/supported-languages) | Text, Images | 1024 | 512 | Cosine Similarity | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed), [Embed Jobs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed-jobs) |
| `embed-multilingual-light-v3.0` | A smaller, faster version of `embed-multilingual-v3.0`. Almost as capable, but a lot faster. Supports multiple languages. | Text, Images | 384 | 512 | Cosine Similarity | [Embed](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed), [Embed Jobs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed-jobs) |

# Cohere Command A+: Launch Guide (May 2026)

Cohere released Command A+ on May 20, 2026: a 218B sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 25B active parameters, Apache 2.0 licensed, that runs on as few as 2 H100 GPUs. Built for sovereign, on-prem enterprise agents with native citations.

 Published 26 May 2026• Updated 05 Oct 2026• 8 min read

**Quick answer.** Cohere Command A+ is a 218B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model (25B active) released May 20, 2026 under Apache 2.0. It runs on as few as 2 H100 GPUs at W4A4 quantization, supports 48 languages and a 128K context window, ships with native citation grounding, and is positioned for sovereign, on-prem enterprise agentic workflows. Weights live on Hugging Face as `CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026`.

Cohere shipped Command A+ on May 20, 2026, and it is the most consequential open-weight release the company has ever made. It is the first Cohere model published under a true Apache 2.0 license, the first to break the 200B-parameter barrier from the lab, and the first to unify reasoning, vision, multilingual, and tool-use behaviour into one set of weights. This guide covers what it is, how it performs, how to deploy it, and when it is the right choice over Llama 4, Qwen 3.5, or DeepSeek V4.

## What is Command A+?

Command A+ is a decoder-only sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformer with **218 billion total parameters and 25 billion active parameters per token**. The model uses 128 experts with 8 activated per token plus one shared expert that runs on every token. It accepts text and images and emits text, reasoning traces, tool calls, and grounded citations.

The headline release specs:

*   **Total / active parameters:** 218B / 25B
*   **Context window:** 128K input tokens, 64K max generation
*   **Languages:** 48 (up from 23 in Command A)
*   **Modalities:** Text + image in; text out
*   **License:** Apache 2.0 (commercial use, no revenue caps, no non-compete)
*   **Weights:**[CohereLabs on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs) in BF16, FP8, and W4A4 quantizations
*   **Minimum hardware:** 2x H100 (W4A4) or 1x B200

Command A+ replaces and consolidates four earlier Cohere models in one set of weights: Command A (text), Command A Reasoning, Command A Vision, and Command A Translate. That consolidation is the practical reason most existing Cohere customers will move to it on the next deployment cycle.

## What changed versus Command A (March 2025)?

Command A landed in March 2025 as a 111B dense model with 256K context, 23 languages, and a Cohere-source-available license that capped commercial use. Command A+ is a different beast:

*   **Architecture:** 111B dense → 218B sparse MoE (25B active). Bigger total capacity, similar serving cost.
*   **Context:** 256K → 128K input + 64K output. A deliberate trade: shorter context but much stronger long-output reasoning and tool-use traces.
*   **Languages:** 23 → 48, including all official EU languages and improved non-European efficiency.
*   **License:** Source-available with revenue caps → Apache 2.0, no caps, no restrictions.
*   **Modalities:** Text → text + vision (charts, PDFs, slides, spreadsheets) in one set of weights.
*   **Citations:** Optional RAG add-on → native grounded citations in every output.
*   **Hardware:** 2x A100/H100 → 2x H100 at W4A4, or 1x B200.

The MoE move is the structural change. Cohere is now spending parameter budget the same way DeepSeek and Qwen do: scale total capacity, keep active-per-token small, and let routing handle specialisation.

## What makes Command A+ different from other open models?

There are three things Command A+ does that no other open frontier model does end-to-end today.

**1. Native citation grounding.** Every generated claim can be tied to an explicit grounding span in the source documents. This is not RAG-on-top; it is trained into the model. For regulated industries (legal, healthcare, finance, public sector) this is the single biggest selling point: you can show your auditor exactly which sentence in which retrieved document supports each output token.

**2. Lossless W4A4 quantization at 218B scale.** Cohere claims (and benchmarks confirm) imperceptible quality differences between BF16, FP8, and the W4A4 4-bit weight / 4-bit activation variant. That is what compresses the model to fit on 2x H100s. Most other open MoE models in this class either don't ship a 4-bit-activation variant at all or take a measurable benchmark hit when they do.

**3. Apache 2.0 with no asterisks.** Llama 4 ships under the Llama Community License (revenue cap, naming clauses). Qwen 3.5 ships under the Tongyi Qianwen License (use-case restrictions). DeepSeek V4 is MIT-leaning but still has model-card limitations. Command A+ is the first model at this capability tier under a permissive, OSI-approved license with zero downstream conditions. For sovereign deployments, that matters more than two benchmark points.

## How does Command A+ compare to Llama 4 and Qwen 3.5?

Cohere's own numbers show large jumps on agentic and reasoning suites versus Command A Reasoning, while staying competitive on raw math. Headline vendor-reported jumps:

*   **τ²-Bench Telecom (agentic):** 37% → 85%
*   **Terminal-Bench Hard (agentic coding):** 3% → 25%
*   **AIME 2025 (math):** 57% → 90%
*   **Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2:** 13.13, versus 6.96 for the original Command A — both measured on the same index version (captured October 2026)

Read the vendor numbers against a neutral composite, though, and the picture is more modest. On **Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index v4.3.2** — the October 2026 rebase, which weights 10 evaluations (AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1) — Command A+ scores **13.13**. That is roughly double the original Command A's 6.96 and ahead of Llama 4 Maverick's 9.99, but it sits below the open-weight leaders on the same version: Qwen3.8 Max 40.15, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 39.82, Qwen3.8 27B 20.15 (33.70 at its Xhigh effort setting), Kimi K2.6 26.98, Gemma 4 26B A4B 16.67. Command A+ is therefore _not_ the top of the open-weight pack on a blended intelligence score. The case for it is licensing, citation grounding, sovereign deployment, and latency — not the composite.

Versus the broader open-weight field:

*   **vs Llama 4 Maverick:** Command A+ wins decisively on agentic / tool-use benchmarks and citation grounding. Llama 4 Scout still wins on raw context length (10M tokens vs 128K) for needle-in-haystack tasks.
*   **vs Qwen 3.5:** Qwen 3.5 ties or edges out Command A+ on pure GPQA Diamond reasoning (88.4% with only 17B active) and is cheaper to host. Command A+ is materially better on multilingual coverage (48 vs ~29) and is the only one of the two with native citations.
*   **vs DeepSeek V4:** DeepSeek V4-Pro still leads on raw code generation (93.5% LiveCodeBench) and on cost-per-token at API providers. Command A+ wins on enterprise features: vision, citations, sovereign deployment story, and Apache 2.0.

If you are picking by use case: **raw coding agent → DeepSeek V4. Cheapest hosted inference → Qwen 3.5. Long-context retrieval → Llama 4 Scout. Auditable enterprise RAG / on-prem → Command A+.**

One latency note worth flagging, because it is where Command A+ genuinely leads. Artificial Analysis measures it at **156 output tokens/second median** with a **0.49-second median time to first chunk** (October 2026 capture). For context, Qwen3.8 27B runs ~51 tok/s and Ring-2.6-1T ~116 tok/s on the same harness. That speed is a direct consequence of 25B active parameters plus W4A4 — and for agentic loops that issue many short tool calls, tokens-per-second and first-chunk latency matter more than peak benchmark scores.

## How do I deploy Command A+?

There are four shipping paths, in increasing order of operational lift.

**1. Cohere's hosted API.** Easiest for prototyping. The model is available through Cohere's API and a free Hugging Face Space demo. Use this to validate the prompt-shape and the citation output, then move to your own infra.

**2. Hugging Face Inference Endpoints.** Pick the `CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4` repo, attach 2x H100s, deploy. Roughly 30 minutes from zero to a private endpoint.

**3. vLLM self-host.** The recommended pattern for production. Requires `vllm >= 0.21.0`, `transformers`, and `cohere_melody >= 0.9.0` (Cohere's parser library for tool calls and reasoning spans). Launch with:

```
vllm serve CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4 \
  -tp 2 \
  --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 \
  --reasoning-parser cohere_command4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Adjust `-tp` (tensor parallelism) to match your GPU count. For 2x H100s, `-tp 2` is the canonical setting.

**4. Air-gapped / sovereign.** Pull the weights once, mirror to an internal registry, deploy in a VPC, on-prem rack, or fully air-gapped environment. The Apache 2.0 license is what makes this clean: no phone-home, no telemetry, no licensing server.

Command A+ is also listed in Microsoft Foundry's model catalogue for customers who already standardised on Azure AI infrastructure.

## What's the licensing?

Apache 2.0. Full stop. You can use, fine-tune, distil, deploy commercially, sell access to, and air-gap Command A+ with no revenue caps, no field-of-use restrictions, and no acceptable-use addenda. Cohere has explicitly framed this as their commitment to sovereign infrastructure: customers running classified, regulated, or critical workloads cannot accept a model whose license can change underneath them. Apache 2.0 closes that risk vector.

The practical impact for builders: Command A+ weights can be fine-tuned on confidential internal data, redistributed inside an organisation, baked into commercial products, or vendored into an on-prem appliance. None of those required a separate license conversation, and none can be revoked.

## When should you choose Command A+?

Pick Command A+ when at least two of the following are true:

*   You are building **RAG with auditability requirements** — legal, healthcare, finance, public sector — and need citation spans on every claim.
*   You need **true sovereign deployment** (VPC, on-prem, air-gapped) and cannot ship data to a hosted API.
*   You are building a **multilingual agent** serving 25+ languages, especially across EU official languages.
*   You want **one set of weights** for reasoning + vision + tool use + translation rather than maintaining a model zoo.
*   You need an Apache 2.0 license, not a community / commercial-with-caveats license.

Skip it if you are optimising for the cheapest possible hosted inference (Qwen 3.5 is cheaper), pure coding agent quality (DeepSeek V4 still leads), or massive single-document context windows beyond 128K (Llama 4 Scout's 10M context wins). For most enterprise teams building agents on private data, Command A+ is now the default open-weight choice.

## FAQ

### Is Command A+ truly open source?

Yes. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license, which is OSI-approved and imposes no revenue caps, naming requirements, or use-case restrictions. This is a stronger open-source posture than Llama 4 (community license) or Qwen 3.5 (Tongyi Qianwen license).

### What hardware do I need to run Command A+?

Minimum 2x NVIDIA H100 GPUs at W4A4 4-bit quantization, or a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200. FP8 needs 4x H100 or 2x B200. BF16 needs 8x H100 or 4x B200. Cohere recommends W4A4 for most deployments because benchmark quality is essentially identical to BF16.

### How does Command A+ handle citations?

Citations are produced natively, not bolted on. The model generates explicit grounding spans that map each claim in the output to specific text spans in the retrieved source documents. This is what makes Command A+ usable in regulated industries where every claim needs an audit trail.

### Can I fine-tune Command A+ on private data?

Yes. The Apache 2.0 license explicitly permits modification, fine-tuning, and redistribution. You can fine-tune on confidential internal data, deploy the fine-tuned weights to your own infrastructure, and use the resulting model commercially without any conversation with Cohere.

### How does Command A+ compare to GPT-5.5 or Claude Opus 4.7?

Not closely, on blended intelligence. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (October 2026), Command A+ scores 13.13 against 38.36 for GPT-5.5, 30.93 for Claude Opus 4.7 and 41.79 for Claude Opus 4.8 — a real gap, not a rounding error. What Command A+ gives you instead is full weight ownership, sovereign and air-gapped deployment, native citation grounding, far lower latency, and Apache 2.0 licensing. If your requirement is auditable RAG on private infrastructure, those matter more than the composite score. If your requirement is maximum reasoning quality, a frontier closed model is still the honest answer.

### What languages does Command A+ support?

48 languages, including all official EU languages plus Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Hebrew, Persian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Indonesian, and more. Cohere specifically improved Arabic dialect matching and non-European-language efficiency in this release.

### Where can I download Command A+?

From Cohere Labs on Hugging Face. The W4A4 quantization is at `CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-w4a4`. BF16 and FP8 variants are published alongside. Also available via Cohere's API and Microsoft Foundry.
