## What is Cohere's business focus and history?

Cohere is a Canadian artificial intelligence company founded in 2019 by Aidan Gomez, Ivan Zhang, and Nick Frosst. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with offices in San Francisco, Montreal, London, New York City, Paris, and Seoul, Cohere specializes in large language models and AI solutions tailored for enterprise applications. The company offers products such as the North platform and Command language models, serving industries including finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and energy. As of 2025, Cohere has raised over $1 billion in funding, with a valuation of $7 billion, and reported annual revenue of $150 million.

# AI Startup Cohere Targets $20 Billion Valuation in Funding Round

By  [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/author/pymnts/ "Posts by PYMNTS")   |  September 11, 2026

|

![Cohere](https://www.pymnts.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Cohere.png?w=620&quality=82)

Artificial intelligence startup [Cohere](https://cohere.com/) is in [advanced talks to raise](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-canadian-ai-firm-cohere-in-advanced-talks-to-raise-up-to-3-billion/) between $2 billion and $3 billion at a valuation of $20 billion, The Globe and Mail reported Friday (Sept. 11).

The deal could close as soon as next week, although it has not been finalized, and the terms could change, according to the report.

If the deal were to close at the reported figures, it would become the largest on record by a private Canadian startup and would make Cohere one of Canada’s most valuable tech companies, per the report.

Reached by PYMNTS, Cohere said in an emailed statement: “We don’t comment on speculation but can confirm that Cohere has seen strong inbound interest from investors as part of our Series E process. The level of engagement reflects broad confidence in our strategy, product momentum and global demand for sovereign AI. We’ll share full details once the process formally concludes.”

[Cohere was valued](https://cohere.com/blog/september-2025-funding-round) at $7 billion in September 2025 when it raised an additional $100 million as part of the second close of a funding round. A month earlier, in August 2025, the company was valued at $6.8 billion when it raised $500 million in [funding](https://www.pymnts.com/news/investment-tracker/2025/ai-startup-cohere-raises-500-million-hires-former-meta-and-uber-executives/).

When announcing the second close, Cohere said in a blog post that it was scaling its operations across the North America, Asia-Pacific (APAC), and Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) regions to meet growing demand for secure and sovereign AI solutions.

Cohere said in the post that its AI models are designed to power agentic business operations and that its platform is purpose-built for businesses and governments that handle sensitive data. Its agents are active in the finance, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications, energy and government sectors.

Cohere Chief Financial Officer [Francois Chadwick](https://www.linkedin.com/in/francois-chadwick-9405474) said in the September 2025 post that the strong investor demand in the second close endorsed the company’s momentum in deploying secure and sovereign AI for enterprises.

“We believe that Cohere’s AI solutions are meeting an ignored demand in the market for technology that truly improves the efficiency of businesses and governments, while keeping full control of their data in their own hands,” Chadwick said in the post.

## Key Highlights

*   Cohere demonstrated exceptional revenue growth, with annualized revenue reaching $100 million by May 2025 and $150 million by October 2025—nearly 4x growth from the $35 million run rate in March 2024. The company expects to exceed $200 million by year-end 2025. In August 2025, Cohere secured a $500 million funding round at a $6.8 billion valuation, followed by a $100 million second close in September 2025 that increased the valuation to $7 billion. Total funding now exceeds $1.6 billion.

*   The company’s technology foundation is built on significant intellectual capital, with co-founder Aidan Gomez having co-authored the seminal “Attention Is All You Need” paper that introduced transformer architecture. In August 2025, Cohere launched North into general availability—a security-first agentic AI platform that integrates the Command family of models, Compass search, and customizable AI agents into a unified workspace. North can be deployed on-premises, in private clouds, or in air-gapped environments with as few as two GPUs, meeting compliance standards including GDPR, SOC 2, and ISO 27001. Internal benchmarks show North outperforms Microsoft Copilot and Google Vertex AI in retrieval-augmented generation accuracy across finance, HR, customer support, and IT tasks.

*   Cohere has secured strategic investments from major tech players including Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Oracle, and Cisco Systems, along with PSP Investments, Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP), Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC), and Nexxus Capital Management. The Canadian government committed up to C$240 million in December 2024 for AI data center construction, and in August 2025 signed a memorandum of understanding with Cohere to deploy AI across government operations. In September 2025, AMD expanded its partnership with Cohere, certifying the Command family of models to run on AMD Instinct GPUs—positioning Cohere as a key partner in AMD’s AI ecosystem alongside its investment role.

*   The company’s enterprise-focused strategy emphasizes data privacy and security, offering flexible deployment options including on-premises installations, while supporting over 100 languages – key differentiators in the competitive AI landscape. Major 2025 customer wins include: RBC (co-developed North for Banking), Dell (North integrated into Dell AI Factory), Bell Canada (sovereign AI services partnership), LG CNS (Korean enterprise deployment), Ensemble Health Partners (healthcare agentic AI), and the Canadian government. The July 2025 Bell Canada partnership positions Cohere as the backbone of Canada’s sovereign AI infrastructure, with Bell deploying Cohere technology on its data centers and offering AI solutions to government and enterprise clients.

*   Despite strong growth, investors should note significant risk factors including intense competition from vastly well-capitalized competitors like OpenAI (reportedly valued at $500 billion as of late 2025), Anthropic (valued at $183 billion), Google, and Microsoft, along with potential regulatory challenges in the rapidly evolving AI sector. Cohere’s $7 billion valuation, while impressive, is a fraction of its American competitors’ valuations, and the company must continue demonstrating that its enterprise-focused, privacy-first approach can compete effectively against models with consumer scale. The August 2025 hire of former Uber CFO Francois Chadwick suggests preparation for potential public markets, but IPO timing and valuation remain uncertain.

## Cohere's Founding

Cohere was founded at the University of Toronto in 2019 by [Aidan Gomez, Nick Frosst, and Ivan Zhang](https://cohere.com/about), who shared a vision for the future of artificial intelligence. Gomez and Frosst had cut their teeth at Google Brain, while Zhang had previously collaborated with Gomez on groundbreaking [research at FOR.ai](http://for.ai/).

What set Cohere apart from the start was the deep technical expertise of its founding team. Notably, Gomez had co-authored the revolutionary 2017 paper “[Attention Is All You Need](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/file/3f5ee243547dee91fbd053c1c4a845aa-Paper.pdf),” which introduced the transformer architecture—a breakthrough that would reshape the entire field of AI. This prestigious background gave the young company immediate credibility in the competitive AI landscape.

In its early days, Cohere focused on building robust infrastructure for training large language models, a decision that would prove prescient. When OpenAI released GPT-3, it validated Cohere’s strategic direction and helped sharpen their product focus. The company has since flourished, establishing a global presence with offices across major tech hubs including Toronto, San Francisco, London, New York City, and—as of 2026—Montreal, Paris, and Seoul.

In January 2025, [the company launched North](https://cohere.com/north), a security-first AI workspace platform designed to compete directly with Microsoft Copilot and Google Vertex AI. North reached general availability in August 2025, with customers including RBC, Dell, LG CNS, and Ensemble Health Partners.

Major partnerships accelerated Cohere’s growth throughout 2025. In July, [Bell Canada announced a strategic partnership](https://cohere.com/blog/bell-partnership) to provide sovereign AI services to Canadian government and enterprise customers, with Bell deploying Cohere technology on its data center infrastructure. In August, the Canadian government signed a memorandum of understanding with Cohere to explore AI deployment across government operations. Dell integrated North into its AI Factory stack, enabling customers to purchase servers pre-loaded with Cohere’s platform.

## What Cohere Does: Core Products and Services

From transforming enterprise workflows to pioneering multilingual AI capabilities, Cohere has emerged as a powerhouse in the enterprise AI landscape. The company’s innovative product suite seamlessly integrates advanced language models with practical business solutions, enabling organizations of all sizes to harness AI’s potential while prioritizing security and scalability. Here’s an in-depth look at how Cohere is revolutionizing enterprise AI through its diverse portfolio of products and services.

### Core Language Models: Command Family

At the heart of Cohere’s innovation lies the Command family of large language models—a testament to their mastery of transformer architecture. Their flagship model, [Command R+](https://cohere.com/command), sets new standards in language processing with its exceptional accuracy and impressive 128,000-token context window, enabling enterprises to tackle increasingly complex language tasks with unprecedented precision.

### Enterprise APIs

Cohere’s sophisticated [API ecosystem](https://cohere.com/blog/new-api-v2) transforms raw AI power into practical business solutions:

*   Generate API: Powers sophisticated text generation capabilities, enabling dynamic chatbot interactions, automated content creation, and summarization.
*   Embed API: Produces precise text embeddings, essential for advanced applications like semantic search and nuanced text classification.
*   Rerank API: Revolutionizes search functionality by intelligently prioritizing results based on contextual relevance.

### Deployment Solutions

Understanding that enterprise needs vary widely, Cohere offers [unparalleled flexibility in deployment options](https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/the-cohere-platform). Whether through cloud-based solutions or on-premises installations, organizations maintain complete control over their data while accessing advanced AI capabilities. This versatility has proven invaluable for companies seeking to enhance customer service, optimize search functionality, and unlock insights from vast text repositories.

### Multilingual Capabilities

In today’s global marketplace, Cohere stands out with its exceptional multilingual prowess. Supporting over 100 languages, including traditionally underserved ones, their models break down language barriers in international business. The [state-of-the-art Aya initiative](https://cohere.com/research/aya), featuring two open-weight models, further demonstrates their commitment to advancing non-English language processing.

### North AI Workspace Platform

[North](https://cohere.com/north) represents Cohere’s vision for the future of enterprise AI integration. This innovative platform seamlessly weaves together LLMs, advanced search capabilities, and customizable AI agents, creating a unified workspace where AI enhances rather than complicates daily operations. Through North, organizations can deploy tailored AI solutions that align perfectly with their unique workflows and objectives.

### Research and Development

Cohere maintains its competitive edge through consistent research and development, regularly introducing model improvements and expanding their technological capabilities. This dedication to innovation, combined with their enterprise-focused approach and extensive language support, positions Cohere as a leading force in the enterprise AI sector.

## How Cohere Makes Money: The Business Model

Cohere has established itself as a leader in the AI industry through its sophisticated API offerings, enabling businesses of all sizes to harness the power of artificial intelligence. Their structured pricing model reflects their commitment to accessibility, starting with a Free Plan for developers and small projects, scaling up to a Production Plan with enhanced capabilities, and culminating in a comprehensive Enterprise Plan featuring dedicated model instances and premium support.

At the heart of Cohere’s revenue model lies a precise, usage-based pricing structure. Their [core services are priced competitively](https://cohere.com/pricing), with Command R+ at $2.50 per 1M tokens for input and $10.00 per 1M tokens for output, Embedding at $0.10 per 1M token, and Rerank capabilities at $2.00 per one thousand search units.

The numbers tell a compelling story of Cohere’s market success. The company demonstrated impressive growth, with annualized revenue reaching [$35 million by March 2024](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/technology/2024/07/22/ai-startup-cohere-valued-at-55-billion-in-new-funding-round/), nearly tripling from $13 million at the close of 2023.

The company crossed $100 million in annualized revenue by May 2025—nearly tripling from the $35 million run rate in March 2024. By October 2025, [annualized revenue reached $150 million](http://bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-10-20/nvidia-backed-cohere-to-offer-secondary-sale-of-employee-shares), and Cohere has told investors it expects to exceed $200 million by year-end 2025 going into 2026.

In the B2B landscape, Cohere has carved out a distinctive niche, delivering enterprise solutions across diverse sectors including finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and energy. Their AI models excel in critical business functions, from document summarization and content generation to sophisticated chatbot implementations and advanced search capabilities.

Strategic partnerships have played a pivotal role in Cohere’s expansion. Their [collaboration with Google Cloud](https://techcrunch.com/2021/11/17/google-cloud-teams-up-with-nlp-startup-cohere-on-multi-year-partnership/)provides robust infrastructure support, while integrations with Oracle’s business applications and MongoDB have accelerated enterprise AI adoption. These alliances have strengthened Cohere’s position as a trusted enterprise AI provider. What sets Cohere apart in the competitive AI marketplace is their unwavering focus on enterprise-grade, customizable AI models that prioritize data security and privacy. Their flexible deployment options, including cloud-agnostic solutions and on-premises installations, particularly appeal to industries with stringent data regulations.

The company continues to innovate and expand its horizons. Their [latest venture, North](https://venturebeat.com/ai/cohere-launches-north-to-redefine-enterprise-ai-with-security-and-customization-at-its-core/), represents a significant step forward in enterprise AI integration. This AI workspace platform seamlessly combines LLMs, search capabilities, and AI agents, empowering enterprise employees to incorporate AI into their daily workflows. With this strategic move, Cohere is well-positioned to capture an even larger share of the rapidly expanding enterprise AI market.

## Cohere’s 2026 Valuation

Cohere’s 2026 valuation reflects diverse pricing inputs, including the company’s most recent funding round, current fund valuations, and secondary market transactions.

Cohere’s impressive rise in the AI industry has captured the attention of tech giants and investors alike. The company’s enterprise-focused AI solutions have propelled its valuation to a cool $5.5 billion as of July 2024, more than doubling its worth from just a year prior. This dramatic growth came through a substantial [$500 million Series D funding round](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/22/cohere-raises-500m-to-beat-back-generative-ai-rivals/), marking a new chapter in Cohere’s impressive journey. The company’s enterprise-focused AI solutions have propelled its valuation to [$7 billion as of September 2025](https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/24/cohere-hits-7b-valuation-a-month-after-its-last-raise-partners-with-amd/)—making it Canada’s most valuable AI startup—representing approximately 150% growth since July 2024.

The company’s funding trajectory tells a compelling story of accelerating momentum. Starting with a [$40 million Series A round](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/09/07/2292856/0/en/Cohere-Raises-40-Million-in-Series-A-Financing-to-Make-Natural-Language-Processing-Safe-and-Accessible-to-Any-Business.html) in September 2021, Cohere quickly gained traction, securing [$125 million in Series B funding](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/2/16/2386297/0/en/Cohere-Raises-125M-Series-B-to-Fuel-Rapid-Platform-Development-and-Scale-International-Footprint.html) just months later. By June 2023, the company had attracted [$270 million in Series C funding](https://techcrunch.com/2023/06/08/ai-startup-cohere-now-valued-at-over-2-1b-raises-270m/), and its latest Series D round brought total investments to nearly $1 billion.

What makes Cohere particularly intriguing is its roster of strategic investors. Industry powerhouses like Nvidia, AMD, Salesforce, Oracle, and Cisco Systems have all placed their bets on the company’s potential. The participation of PSP Investments, a major Canadian pension investment manager, adds another layer of institutional confidence in Cohere’s long-term prospects.

Recent growth metrics and strategic developments may make a strong case for considering Cohere as an investment target:

### Market Leadership in Enterprise AI

Cohere has emerged as a compelling investment prospect in the enterprise AI landscape, particularly in the realm of natural language processing and machine learning solutions. The company’s focus on delivering customizable, enterprise-grade AI models has secured its position as a frontrunner in this rapidly expanding market.

### Strong Revenue Growth

The company’s growth trajectory tells a remarkable story, with annualized revenue reaching $150 million by October 2025—representing approximately 5-6x growth from the $35 million run rate in March 2024. These relationships may not only validate Cohere’s technology but may also provide robust channels for market expansion.

### Emphasis on Capital Efficiency

What sets Cohere apart is its commitment to [capital efficiency](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/09/cohere-sees-big-ai-opportunity-in-enterprise-away-from-chatgpt.html). Further strengthening Cohere’s position is substantial government support, particularly from Canada. The commitment of up to [C$240 million in funding](https://www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/news/2024/12/deputy-prime-minister-announces-240-million-for-cohere-to-scale-up-ai-compute-capacity.html) for a multi-billion dollar AI data center demonstrates strong institutional confidence in the company’s vision and provides essential infrastructure for future growth. Although Cohere is well-positioned to disrupt traditional AI companies through its innovative language models and artificial intelligence capabilities, the company faces several material risks. As an AI technology provider primarily serving enterprise clients, its success depends heavily on navigating complex regulatory frameworks, securing stable contract revenue, and maintaining technological advantages in a competitive landscape. Rapid AI advancement can significantly impact enterprise AI spending priorities and create market opportunities, while simultaneously introducing operational challenges and computational resource volatility.

Before investing in Cohere, potential investors should evaluate several critical risks and challenges (the following examples _do not_ encompass all potential investment risks):

### Competitive Landscape

The dynamic landscape of artificial intelligence presents both opportunities and significant challenges for Cohere as it navigates its path forward. The company faces fierce competition from established players like OpenAI and Anthropic and tech giants such as Google and Microsoft, making continuous innovation not just beneficial but essential for survival in this rapidly evolving market.

### Regulatory Environment

The regulatory environment adds another layer of complexity to Cohere’s business landscape. As governments worldwide grapple with the implications of AI technology, new regulations could reshape the company’s operational framework and business model. Staying ahead of these regulatory changes while maintaining compliance requires significant resources and adaptability.

### Technical Vulnerabilities

Technical challenges inherent to AI systems pose their own set of risks. Issues such as model biases, inaccuracies, or unexpected outputs could potentially damage Cohere’s reputation and expose the company to legal vulnerabilities. Managing these technical risks requires constant vigilance and robust quality control measures.

### Talent Retention

The company’s success is inextricably linked to its human capital, particularly its ability to attract and retain top AI talent in an increasingly competitive market, especially against more well-capitalized competitors. In September 2025, Sara Hooker departed as head of Cohere Labs, the company’s nonprofit research arm, after serving since its 2022 founding. Cohere Labs is now led by Marzieh Fadaee. While leadership transitions are normal, the departure illustrates the ongoing challenge of retaining top researchers when competitors like Meta are offering unprecedented compensation packages to attract AI talent. The departure of additional key team members could significantly impact Cohere’s innovation capabilities and growth trajectory.

### Market Dynamics

Market sentiment in the AI sector can shift rapidly, influenced by technological breakthroughs, public perception, and broader economic trends. These fluctuations could affect Cohere’s valuation and its ability to secure future funding, making it crucial for investors to consider the volatile nature of the AI market when evaluating investment opportunities.

## The Future Outlook of Cohere

As artificial intelligence continues to reshape the global technology landscape, Cohere stands poised to capture a significant share of this burgeoning market. The company’s 2025 performance demonstrates exceptional momentum. Annualized revenue reached $150 million by October 2025—approximately 5-6x growth from March 2024—with expectations to exceed $200 million by year-end. The $600 million raised in 2025 at valuations up to $7 billion provides substantial capital for continued expansion.

Several emerging trends align perfectly with Cohere’s strategic direction. The company may be well-positioned to serve the increasing AI demands across healthcare, finance, and manufacturing

# Cohere seeks $500m funding to advance AI development

![](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/885c8adb9235a516b21e119ab7f319add8f854dc18dc78bdff518ac7c614afa2/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fverdict_626%2Fbbd9f5d270840ff932af606289728169)

With the funding round · Verdict

GlobalData

2 min read

Cohere, a Canadian artificial intelligence start-up, is reportedly seeking to raise more than $500m (C$685m) in a new funding round.

This move aims to strengthen its position in the competitive AI landscape, alongside industry leaders such as OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic.

Cohere is targeting a valuation of more than $5.5bn, reported *Financial Times*, citing sources familiar with the discussions.

According to the media report, the valuation could potentially reach between $6bn and $6.5bn, although discussions remain in the early stages.

This anticipated funding would position Cohere among the most valuable start-ups in the AI sector, despite trailing behind US competitors that have seen significant valuation increases.

In April 2025, OpenAI achieved a $300bn valuation, up from $157bn in 2024, while Anthropic's funding round in March increased its valuation to $61.5bn.

Cohere was founded by former Google researchers, including CEO Aidan Gomez, a co-author of the influential "Attention Is All You Need" paper, which introduced the transformer AI architecture.

Unlike its competitors, Cohere has not launched a consumer-facing app, instead it is focusing on enterprise and privacy-centric solutions.

The company has developed "open" models like the Aya multilingual models, accessible for developers to build upon, entering a market with competitors such as Meta and start-ups Mistral and DeepSeek.

Cohere's founders, including Gomez, Nick Frosst, and Ivan Zhang, are also pursuing contracts with tech giants such as Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, which offer their own AI models to enterprises.

Cohere has doubled its annual recurring revenue in the past four months, surpassing $100m last month.

"A lot of the consumer adoption happened right away," said a source close to Cohere.

"Enterprise tends to be slower in adoption but stickier in terms of users. Companies aren't known to adopt tech early."

The development of advanced AI models demands significant financial investment for training and computing power. Nearly three years after OpenAI's ChatGPT sparked the AI boom, investors are eager to see returns on their investments in AI model creators.

Cohere has also launched North, a platform enabling businesses to build AI agents for office tasks, although it is currently available to a limited number of customers.

In December 2024, it was reported that Cohere [plans to build an](https://www.verdict.co.uk/cohere-data-centre-canada/) 'multibillion-dollar' AI data centre in Canada with financial support from the Canadian government.

"Cohere seeks $500m funding to advance AI development" was originally created and published by [Verdict](https://www.verdict.co.uk/cohere-500m-funding-to-advance-ai-development/), a GlobalData owned brand.

# Cohere $2B-$3B at $20B Valuation: The Sovereign AI Lab Raises a Late-Stage Round Outside the US-China Axis

Lena Park

4 min read

## The Sovereign Alternative

When the Globe and Mail reported September 11 that Cohere is in advanced talks to raise between $2 billion and $3 billion at a $20 billion valuation, the headline numbers were striking enough: a nearly threefold jump from the company's $7 billion valuation just twelve months prior, and the largest funding round on record for a private Canadian startup if it closes. But the number itself is not the story. The story is who is writing the check, and what that says about where AI capital is flowing when it leaves the United States.

The Canadian government is participating directly. Ottawa committed up to CA$240 million through its Sovereign AI Compute Strategy in December 2024 – the first investment through the $2 billion program designed to build domestic compute capacity. Cohere confirmed strong inbound interest as part of its Series E process but declined to comment on specifics. The deal is not finalized; terms could shift.

## Three Labs, Three Exit Strategies

Cohere's raise must be read against the broader capital landscape. OpenAI closed $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation in March 2026, building itself into a compute infrastructure utility. Anthropic is targeting a $100 billion IPO at a $2 trillion valuation, with Nvidia in talks for a $10 billion anchor investment. We tracked this divergence in three labs, three exit strategies – the AI IPO wave is not one story.

Cohere is the third path. Not the capital-intensive, consumer-facing infrastructure play of OpenAI. Not the clean-balance-sheet, public-market exit of Anthropic. Instead, a sovereign industrial policy model: state-backed capital, enterprise-private deployments, and a Canada-Germany axis as geopolitical moat.

## The Canada-Germany Axis

The April 2026 merger with Aleph Alpha – structured as roughly 90% Cohere, 10% Aleph Alpha – was not a typical tech acquisition. It was a diplomatic arrangement. The Canada-Germany Sovereign Technology Alliance, signed earlier in 2026, provided the framework. German Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger attended the Berlin announcement alongside Canada's Minister of AI Evan Solomon. The Schwarz Group committed $600 million as Series E lead, providing access to its STACKIT sovereign cloud and an €11 billion data center investment near Berlin.

Cohere reportedly rejected offers to reincorporate in the United States. The decision to remain Canadian-incorporated, with dual headquarters in Toronto and Berlin, trades the potential for a Silicon Valley-scale exit for the stability of state-backed support and a clear mandate to serve regulated sectors.

## The Financial Profile

The numbers tell a different story than the US frontier labs. Cohere reported $240 million in annual recurring revenue as of February 2026, surpassing its 2025 target of $200 million by 20%. Gross margins sit around 70%. But the structurally significant figure is that 85% of revenue comes from private deployments – not public cloud API access, but on-premise and private-cloud installations for enterprise and government clients including Oracle, Fujitsu, RBC, LG, Notion, SAP, Dell, and McKinsey.

This is a fundamentally different business than selling tokens through a public API. Private deployments require bespoke integration, ongoing support contracts, and localized infrastructure. The labor intensity is higher. The margins are tighter than standardized SaaS. But the switching costs are also higher, and the client relationships are stickier.

## What the Clean Story Obscures

The sovereign AI thesis is compelling, but it rests on a premise that deserves scrutiny: that governments and enterprises will pay a sustained premium for data sovereignty when cheaper, more capable alternatives exist on public infrastructure. The part that gets hidden is who absorbs the risk if sovereign demand proves shallower than McKinsey's projected $600 billion market.

Cohere's $240 million ARR, while growing, implies a revenue multiple of roughly 83x at the reported $20 billion valuation. OpenAI's $25 billion run rate at $852 billion is a 34x multiple. The market is pricing Cohere's sovereign premium at more than twice OpenAI's – a bet that state-backed enterprise demand can sustain a growth trajectory independent of the consumer and developer markets that drive US frontier lab economics.

Whether that bet pays off depends on execution under constraints that US competitors do not face: bilateral regulatory alignment between Canada and Germany, sustained government procurement commitments, and the operational complexity of maintaining private deployments across two continents. If the demand for sovereign control is deep enough, Cohere has a structural moat. If it is not, the company is building expensive infrastructure for a market that may not materialize at the scale the valuation requires.

## What to Watch

The composition of the final investor syndicate will reveal how much of this round is driven by market conviction versus strategic state interest. Further Canadian or German government participation beyond the initial CA$240 million commitment would signal deeper industrial policy integration. The timing – the deal could close as soon as next week per the Globe and Mail – and the split between cash and compute commitments will determine whether this is a capital raise or a sovereignty pact dressed as one.

 Share [![Image 3: linkedin](https://www.investpsp.com/static/assets/images/icons/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.investpsp.com/en/news/fresh-funding-enables-cohere-to-accelerate-its-global-expansion-and-build-the-next-generation-of-secure-enterprise-and-sovereign-ai-solutions/)

Fresh funding enables Cohere to accelerate its global expansion and build the next generation of secure enterprise and sovereign AI solutions.

_Company strengthens its leadership team with the additions of former Head of Meta’s Fundamental AI Research and LLM pioneer Joelle Pineau as Chief AI Officer and former Uber exec François Chadwick as CFO_

Today, we’re excited to announce Cohere’s latest $500M raise at a $6.8B valuation in an oversubscribed round led by Radical Ventures and Inovia Capital, with additional participation from existing investors including AMD Ventures, NVIDIA, PSP Investments, and Salesforce Ventures, as well as new investors, including Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (“HOOPP”), among others.

The new capital will enable us to accelerate our efforts to make businesses and governments around the world vastly more efficient, simplifying tedious tasks through agentic AI solutions. We aim to free up people to spend their time on the interesting, challenging, and human parts of work–all while prioritizing data security. This represents a security-first category of enterprise AI that is simply not being met by repurposed consumer models. Our approach enables us to offer AI solutions that provide local data control, better regulatory compliance, and digital sovereignty.

To support our growth, we’re proud to announce the expansion of our leadership group, adding key expertise to drive our next chapter.

*   **Joelle Pineau will be joining as Chief AI Officer**to advance our cutting-edge research and product development.
*   **François Chadwick will be joining as Chief Financial Officer**to oversee finance and business operations as we accelerate growth to serve our expanding global customer base.

Joelle is a highly respected leader in the AI industry and will be based in our Montréal office. She is a Professor at the School of Computer Science at McGill University and as a core member of Mila, the Québec Artificial Intelligence Institute. She was previously Meta’s VP of AI Research, leading its Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) team.

François is a proven finance and technology executive who will be based in our San Francisco office. He has held key corporate leadership roles, including serving as Uber’s acting CFO, helping scale finance operations globally and playing a leadership role during the company’s IPO. François most recently rejoined KPMG, advising high-growth tech companies, after serving as CFO at Shield AI.

This fresh funding follows a year of accelerated growth through strategic partnerships, and the launch of North, our security-first agentic AI platform. On the strategic partnership front, we now work with global leaders, including Oracle, Dell, RBC, Bell, Fujitsu, LG CNS, SAP, and Ensemble Health Partners to deliver transformative solutions across critical industries such as finance, healthcare, telecommunications, manufacturing, energy, and the public sector.

Key product innovations include a suite of new enterprise-grade applications built on top of our generative model series (Command A and Command A Vision), retrieval models (Embed 4 and Rerank 3.5), and our flagship agentic AI platform, North, that brings them all together.

_"Cohere is becoming the world's chosen partner for integrating AI into their critical industries. We are at a pivotal moment in accelerating the delivery of secure AI that empowers enterprises worldwide, and we’re excited to enter this new phase of expansion alongside our partners. We’re thrilled to welcome Joelle and François, whose experience, talent and insight will be instrumental in continuing Cohere's growth."_**– Aidan Gomez, Co-founder and CEO of Cohere**

_“We have been proud investors and partners with Cohere and its founders since day one, with a vision to deliver leading AI for business. Cohere is fulfilling that promise by building privacy-first, cloud-agnostic models and agentic AI applications that are driving extraordinary productivity gains and ROI to blue-chip enterprises, businesses and governments worldwide. We are co-leading this investment round because this is just the beginning for Cohere.”_**– Jordan Jacobs, Co-Founder and Managing Partner, Radical Ventures**

_“The company's relentless focus on customers' time to value, data privacy, and customization uniquely positions Cohere to lead the enterprise AI adoption, both at home and internationally. We’re proud to continue supporting them as they reshape the future of work.”_**– Patrick Pichette, Partner, Inovia Capital, who will be joining Cohere’s Board of Directors.**

# Canada buying stake in AI firm Cohere to bolster tech sovereignty

By AFP

Published on October 29, 2026 at 20:48

* [![](/modules/custom/afp_homepage/images/social-x.svg) X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.afp.com%2Fen%2Fcanada-buying-stake-ai-firm-cohere-bolster-tech-sovereignty&text=Canada%20buying%20stake%20in%20AI%20firm%20Cohere%20to%20bolster%20tech%20sovereignty)

![Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announces a federal investment of up to C$1.6 billion (US$1.14 billion) in artificial intelligence company Cohere — Alexis Aubin / AFP](/sites/default/files/afp-stories/3d409454aac9d622ae885b51a26e9b36-0-hi.jpg)

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announces a federal investment of up to C$1.6 billion (US$1.14 billion) in artificial intelligence company Cohere — Alexis Aubin / AFP

Canada is investing CAN$1.6 billion ($1 billion) in the AI firm Cohere, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday, a move aimed at strengthening sovereign alternatives to counter US and Chinese AI dominance.

Cohere was founded in Toronto in 2019 and has tried to distinguish itself from artificial intelligence behemoths like OpenAI and Anthropic by focusing on models built for businesses and governments, with less attention paid to consumer applications.

Announcing the investment ahead of a major Canada-EU summit in Montreal, Carney said "this is the moment that will decide where AI is built, how AI is governed, and who AI serves."

"We are not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don't know or by those we don't trust," he added.

The concentration of AI systems in the hands of a few companies carries systemic risks, the prime minister said, warning that while those companies may profess to be "global," they "often prove national in the breach."

Cohere is led by Aidan Gomez, an AI researcher who co-authored a seminal paper that laid the foundations for modern AI systems, underscoring the role of the Canadian AI research ecosystem in the field's development.

The company has already moved to make itself a transatlantic power insulated from US and Chinese control.

In May, Cohere announced a deal to acquire German AI firm Aleph Alpha, creating a combined entity with dual headquarters in Toronto and Berlin, in a deal backed by Ottawa and Berlin.

Gomez told AFP in June that Europe risks "total technological irrelevance" if it fails to develop sovereign capabilities, warning that without home-built technology, everything from defense to productivity will be partly controlled by foreigners.

At Carney's announcement on Thursday, Gomez said the federal investment is part of a funding round targeting CAN$7 billion, which would take the company to a CAN$35.7 billion valuation.

"We are now the largest AI company outside the United States and China," Gomez said.

"Around the world, organizations are looking for technology that they can trust and control, and that reflects their values," he added, pledging that Cohere would be rooted "in Canada always."

In an address to a Montreal research institute before the summit with Carney, EU chief Ursula von der Leyen mentioned the Cohere-Aleph Alpha merger, citing the "strong appetite for teaming up."

Brussels and Ottawa are working on forging unprecedented levels of cooperation, including on AI policy alignment.

# Feds to invest up to $1.6 billion in Canadian AI company Cohere in its $7-billion fundraise

 Yvonne Lau 

Thu, October 29, 2026 at 1:36 p.m. EDT 2 min read

[![Image 7: CANADA-EU-DIPLOMACY-POLITICS](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/dada7b9bdd5eb422b55b921e8f504b2df3beb7acfb9678171badccd7ac3c9cc3/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Ffinancial_post_articles_610%2F70b5c3ef6d226e5f9431256b5e6d6991.jpg)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/dada7b9bdd5eb422b55b921e8f504b2df3beb7acfb9678171badccd7ac3c9cc3/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Ffinancial_post_articles_610%2F70b5c3ef6d226e5f9431256b5e6d6991.jpg)

Prime Minister Mark Carney announces a federal investment of up to $1.6 billion in artificial intelligence company Cohere in Montreal on Oct. 29, 2026. (Credit: Alexis Aubin/AFP via Getty Images) 

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wBZAfh-mwLw)

The federal government says it will invest up to $1.6 billion in Canadian [artificial intelligence](https://financialpost.com/tag/artificial-intelligence/) startup [Cohere Inc.](https://financialpost.com/tag/cohere-inc/) as part of the company's planned $7-billion fundraising round, which is the largest-ever private capital raise in Canada.

The round will value Cohere at $35.7 billion, making it Canada's most valuable private tech company.

Ottawa's investment in Toronto-based Cohere comes alongside the release of its [national security](https://financialpost.com/tag/national-security/) strategy, the first in more than two decades, which said Canada's [sovereignty](https://financialpost.com/tag/sovereignty/) depends on eight key sectors, including emerging technologies such as AI, critical minerals and defence.

"We're not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don't know or by whom we don't trust. We are building it right here, the right way," Prime Minister [Mark Carney](https://financialpost.com/tag/mark-carney/) said in a speech on Thursday. "Cohere has grown from a Toronto startup into a global company. It's a Canadian success story … and now, Canada has a stake in it," he said.

The government is investing in Cohere on a commercial basis alongside Nvidia Corp., BCE Inc. and Germany's Schwarz Group, which is leading the round, as well as others.

Carney said the investment will allow Cohere to create 1,000 new high-paying Canadian technical jobs and direct at least $1.7 billion in new computing infrastructure in the country by 2030. The agreement also ensures that Cohere will "stay Canadian," he said.

AI and Digital Innovation Minister Evan Solomon called the investment "hugely significant," something that will allow Canada to secure a spot as one of four countries — alongside the United States, China and France — with companies developing advanced large language models.

"We see Cohere as a strategically important company to our national security," he said.

The company will use the new funds to advance its large language models and AI tools made for business and government and invest in the infrastructure needed to train its models, Cohere chief financial officer Francois Chadwick said in a statement.

"We will continue to meaningfully scale across North America, EMEA, and APAC to meet growing customer demand," he said.

Cohere in September completed its acquisition of German AI startup Aleph Alpha GmbH, which it said will create a well-positioned transatlantic AI "powerhouse" to scale its business in global markets.

Cohere has promoted its systems as alternatives to Big Tech systems and China's open-source models as governments worldwide rush to advance their sovereign tech.

# Cohere Raises $5 Billion for Alternative AI Vision

By  [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/author/pymnts/ "Posts by PYMNTS")   |  October 29, 2026

|

![Cohere](https://www.pymnts.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Cohere.png?w=620&quality=82)

Canadian artificial intelligence company [Cohere](https://cohere.com/) said in a Thursday (Oct. 29) company blog post that it rejects what it called “[frontier fatalism](https://cohere.com/blog/who-gets-to-build-the-frontier-for-ai).”

That’s its term for the belief that AI will be monopolized by a handful of United States and Chinese tech giants. To offer other countries a sovereign alternative, Cohere announced in the post the initial close of a Series E funding round targeting up to $7 billion Canadian dollars (about $5 billion).

“We will use the funds to build something increasingly essential in AI, a frontier company outside the U.S. and China,” the company said in the post. “Our ambition is to build frontier models that compete with the best in the world, a secure platform that lets institutions own the AI they run on, and cyber defenses democracies can rely on. We don’t have to accept a future of AI run by just a few, and we shouldn’t want one.”

The [Canadian government](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/canada-nvidia-back-cohere-in-round-at-over-20-billion-value) has agreed to invest up to $1.14 billion in Cohere, while the company plans to remain based in Canada and invest around $1.2 billion in new computing infrastructure in the country by 2030, Bloomberg reported Thursday.

“The most powerful AI systems are concentrated in a very small number of companies, in a very small number of countries,” Canadian Prime Minister [Mark Carney](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mark-carney-5b9744205/) said at a news conference Thursday, per Bloomberg. “That concentration carries risks to cost, to resilience and to sovereignty.”

When finished, the round would be the largest private fundraise in Canada’s history, the report said. The funding values Cohere at $20.5 billion, roughly triple its value from last year.

“These investments are critical for the next chapter of our growth,” Cohere Co-Founder and CEO [Aidan Gomez](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aidangomez/) said at the news conference, per the report. “Most importantly, it strengthens Canada’s ability to develop AI on its own terms.”

In other AI news, [Walmart](https://www.walmart.com/) set new rules governing the use of [AI agents](https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2026/walmart-and-amazon-expand-ai-agents-roles-in-shopping-and-work/) in its [eCommerce system](https://www.pymnts.com/commerce/ecommerce/2026/walmart-and-home-depot-set-the-rules-for-ai-shoppers/), PYMNTS reported Thursday. They set who holds the customer, who holds the data and what access will cost.

The [PYMNTS Intelligence](https://www.pymnts.com/pymnts-intelligence/) report “[The Agent Advantage: How Merchants Plan to Win AI Shopping](https://www.pymnts.com/report/study/the-agent-advantage-how-merchants-plan-to-win-ai-shopping/)” found in October that 80% of the merchants would expect to pay a fee or commission on completed agent sales, while less than 30% would offer their full catalog to agents on the same terms as their own site.

Silicon Valley tech CEOs are calling for a slow down of artificial intelligence development — but is that even possible? For The National, CBC's Ashley Fraser looks at what it would take to pace the AI race and why experts say it won't be easy.

Schwarz, which owned more than 20 per cent of Aleph Alpha, spent almost $25 billion on new data centres in Germany. Schwarz ​Digits CEO Christian Müller said the group plans to run Cohere's models on its STACKIT ⁠cloud, calling the investment the next step after the Aleph Alpha ⁠deal.

Cohere has completed only an initial close of the round ⁠and did ⁠not say how much ​has been committed so far or when it expects the round to ​close.

The company said ⁠annual recurring revenue grew 165 per cent year over year as of the third quarter and that its customer count has grown to 300.

# Superwhisper, Cohere partner on meeting recorder for enterprise clients

By [Madison McLauchlan](https://betakit.com/author/madison-mclauchlan/ "Posts by Madison McLauchlan")  October 15, 2026

[Email](mailto:?subject=Superwhisper, Cohere partner on meeting recorder for enterprise clients&body=https://betakit.com/superwhisper-cohere-partner-on-meeting-recorder-to-challenge-enterprise-clients/)   [Share on LinkedIn](http://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://betakit.com/superwhisper-cohere-partner-on-meeting-recorder-to-challenge-enterprise-clients/&title=Superwhisper%2C+Cohere+partner+on+meeting+recorder+for+enterprise+clients&source=BetaKit)   [Share on X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?original_referer=https://betakit.com/superwhisper-cohere-partner-on-meeting-recorder-to-challenge-enterprise-clients/&text=Superwhisper%2C+Cohere+partner+on+meeting+recorder+for+enterprise+clients&tw_p=tweetbutton&url=https://betakit.com/superwhisper-cohere-partner-on-meeting-recorder-to-challenge-enterprise-clients/&via=BetaKit)   [Share on Reddit](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https://betakit.com/superwhisper-cohere-partner-on-meeting-recorder-to-challenge-enterprise-clients/&title=Superwhisper%2C+Cohere+partner+on+meeting+recorder+for+enterprise+clients)   [Share on BlueSky](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Superwhisper%2C+Cohere+partner+on+meeting+recorder+for+enterprise+clients%20https://betakit.com/superwhisper-cohere-partner-on-meeting-recorder-to-challenge-enterprise-clients/)

![The Superwhisper team.](https://cdn.betakit.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/superwhisper-team-770x513.webp "Superwhisper team | BetaKit")

Using Cohere models, meeting transcription and summaries can run locally on users’ devices.

Superwhisper is partnering with Cohere to launch a local meeting recorder, putting the consumer AI dictation tool in competition with enterprise meeting assistant companies like Granola and Otter.

The companies, which are both headquartered in Toronto, announced on Thursday that Superwhisper users can now access Cohere’s AI models to record and transcribe meetings, allowing them to take advantage of the enterprise AI company’s smaller language models, which are trained with far fewer parameters than large language models. Cohere’s [Transcribe model](https://betakit.com/qa-behind-the-scenes-of-coheres-new-ai-transcription-model/) will transcribe what was said, while its [Tiny Aya model](https://betakit.com/from-amharic-to-zulu-coheres-new-multilingual-ai-model-supports-more-than-70-languages/) will provide meeting summaries and action items.

> “Having our core audience realize the power of a tool like this is going to be big for our growth strategy.”
>
> Brendan James, Superwhisper

Notably, using this feature with Cohere’s models lets it run locally on a user’s device, without storing that data with Superwhisper, the company said. Meeting recorder competitors such as [Otter](http://otter.ai) have seen legal action alleging privacy breaches, including a lawsuit claiming that it [deceptively recorded and stored](https://www.npr.org/2025/08/15/g-s1-83087/otter-ai-transcription-class-action-lawsuit) private user conversations. Otter was also embroiled in a controversy in an Ontario hospital when sensitive patient data was [mistakenly shared](https://www.hrreporter.com/focus-areas/automation-ai/ai-bot-sends-confidential-info-to-ontario-hospital-patients-after-recording-doctors-meeting-ipc/393766) with dozens of people.

“Privacy has always been a main point of our brand, because dictation is obviously so sensitive,” Superwhisper head of growth Brendan James said in an interview.

Founded in 2023 by [PartnerStack](https://betakit.com/appdirect-acquires-partnerstack-to-build-unified-platform-for-partner-led-growth/) co-founder Neil Chudleigh, Superwhisper is on a mission to allow people to do work primarily through voice dictation instead of typing on keyboards. The startup’s platform allows users to select different AI models of varying sizes to perform voice-to-text transcription, and previously [partnered with Cohere](https://betakit.com/superwhisper-partners-with-cohere-for-all-canadian-voice-to-text-ai/) to use its [AI transcription model](https://betakit.com/qa-behind-the-scenes-of-coheres-new-ai-transcription-model/). It also released its own small, open-weight transcription cleanup model, S1, which appears as a default when users sign up.

Superwhisper already had a setting for meeting recording in its consumer dictation product, James said, but it wasn’t the easiest to find and was mostly employed by technically minded users. The team felt that with Cohere’s locally run models, they could offer an edge over other transcription services that are largely cloud-based (meaning the data is stored in the cloud rather than on a user’s device).

“This tool is our biggest swing at a full-company suite of products,” James said.

The tool doesn’t join meetings as an individual participant (a phenomenon some tech leaders have [complained about](https://x.com/tobi/status/1983295626952749189?s=20)), and James said this was intentional because the team finds it “invasive.” Canadian meeting-assistant startup [Fellow](https://betakit.com/fellow-surpasses-5000-customers-after-rebooting-for-the-ai-era/) works similarly and has called the feature “botless recording.”

**RELATED:** [**Cohere to acquire Czech AI cybersecurity firm Aisle, set up new cyber division**](https://betakit.com/cohere-to-acquire-czech-ai-cybersecurity-firm-aisle-set-up-new-cyber-division/)

With the launch, Superwhisper is envisioning a push toward more enterprise clients. A significant portion of its user base consists of software developers dictating instructions to AI coding assistants—essentially, speaking code into terminals. The idea is to have its most frequent users try out the new tool and encourage adoption across their companies.

“Meeting tools are a dime a dozen. There’s so much competition,” James said. “Having our core audience realize the power of a tool like this is going to be big for our growth strategy.”

The company currently has professionals at big-name tech companies OpenAI, Meta, and Shopify using its transcription tools, James claimed. Earlier this summer, Superwhisper told *BetaKit* that its revenue split used to be mostly from individual users, but has increasingly grown toward enterprise plans.

Superwhisper prices its pro subscriptions at monthly, annual, or a one-time flat rate, but for the moment, it isn’t charging a premium for access to the meeting tool. In the near future, James said, they’ll likely revisit enterprise pricing.

# Cohere to acquire AISLE to advance cyber-resilient sovereign AI

By

[Cybersecurity Insiders](https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/author/silvernine25/)

-

[[ Join Cybersecurity Insiders ]](https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/join-cybersecurity-insiders/)

161

![](https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/wp-content/uploads/Secure-AI-Partnership-in-a-Connected-World-696x392.png "Secure-AI-Partnership-in-a-Connected-World")

*By combining sovereign AI and cybersecurity expertise, Cohere to launch Cohere Cyber, expanding its platform to help enterprises and governments secure AI systems in an increasingly complex threat landscape*

Today Cohere announced a proposed agreement to acquire AISLE, the company building autonomous systems to discover and remediate previously unknown vulnerabilities in critical software.

The proposed transaction represents another important step in Cohere’s mission to build the world’s leading sovereign AI platform, combining frontier AI models, agentic applications, secure deployment infrastructure, and advanced security capabilities that enable organizations to deploy AI with confidence.

It also reflects our continued investment in Europe. Following our acquisition of Reliant AI and partnership with Aleph Alpha, the addition of AISLE would deepen our presence across the region and strengthen European AI and cybersecurity capabilities that help protect critical infrastructure, governments, and highly regulated industries around the world.

**Security is becoming the defining challenge of enterprise AI**

As organizations move AI from experimentation to production, security has become one of the most important factors determining successful adoption.

Enterprises and governments are increasingly navigating complex requirements around data protection, governance, regulatory compliance, software vulnerabilities, and the risks associated with more autonomous AI systems. At the same time, they are looking for AI partners that can deliver the flexibility to operate in private cloud, on-premises, and fully air-gapped environments without compromising security or control.

Addressing these security challenges requires more than powerful models. It requires a full-stack approach that brings together AI, cybersecurity, governance, and secure deployment. That’s why we’re excited about the opportunity to bring AISLE’s expertise into Cohere.

**Why AISLE**

Founded in 2024, AISLE has developed innovative AI systems capable of discovering, validating and helping remediate previously unknown vulnerabilities in complex production software. Its approach combines increasingly capable foundation models with specialized security expertise, large-scale code analysis, rigorous validation and automated remediation.

In its first year out of stealth, AISLE discovered more than [500 previously unknown vulnerabilities assigned CVEs](https://aisle.com/blog/aisle-year-on-the-cyber-frontier) across more than 100 codebases, including all 12 vulnerabilities in OpenSSL’s January security release and [18 of the 24 CVEs in curl’s latest release](https://aisle.com/blog/one-aisle-curl-audit-produced-24-cves-18-ship-today). These real-world zero-day vulnerabilities are independently reviewed by the relevant software maintainers, demonstrating the growing capabilities of autonomous AI security systems.

AISLE’s results also highlight an important insight: the capabilities of a foundation model and the specialized system built around it can reinforce each other. By bringing AISLE’s autonomous security research closer to Cohere’s frontier-model development and training, we see an opportunity to build more capable cybersecurity systems while exploring how difficult, verifiable security problems can help evaluate and improve future models.

**Founders take Cohere leadership roles within newly-formed Cohere Cyber, with Prague set for expansion**

AISLE’s team is joining Cohere, with its three founders taking leadership roles spanning cybersecurity, corporate security, AI security research and frontier model development.

Ondrej Vlcek will become Senior Vice President, Cohere Cyber, and will lead the newly-established global cybersecurity business. Jaya Baloo will become Cohere’s Chief Information Security Officer, leading security across the company. Stanislav Fort will become Vice President, AI Security, joining Cohere’s core model research and training efforts and leading its AI security research.

Cohere also plans to make a substantial long-term investment in Prague, expanding AISLE’s existing presence and establishing the city as its global center for AI cybersecurity and autonomous security systems.

**Strengthening Europe’s role in the future of AI**

Europe is becoming increasingly important in the development of sovereign AI. Governments and enterprises across the region are seeking technology partners that can deliver advanced AI capabilities while meeting stringent requirements around security, privacy, compliance, and data sovereignty. Cohere has made significant investments to support those needs, and this deal would further expand our ability to serve customers across Europe and globally.

**What this means for customers**

AISLE’s technology will strengthen Cohere’s ability to help customers build and operate secure, cyber-resilient AI systems.

The combined capabilities are expected to enhance Cohere’s ability to:

* Deliver advanced security and threat detection capabilities across enterprise and public sector deployments.
* Strengthen governance, monitoring, and observability for AI agents and autonomous workflows.
* Improve protections for sensitive organizational data and mission-critical systems.
* Support secure AI deployments across private cloud, on-premises, and fully air-gapped environments.
* Advance the development of cyber-resilient AI systems capable of identifying, prioritizing, and responding to emerging threats.

**Looking ahead**

At Cohere, we’ve long believed that organizations should maintain control over their AI strategy, data, infrastructure and governance. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in critical workflows, securing the software these systems depend on is becoming just as important.

Increasingly capable AI systems are transforming both cybersecurity and the threats organizations face, and defensive capabilities must advance just as quickly. By combining AISLE’s autonomous vulnerability research with Cohere’s frontier models and sovereign AI platform, we aim to make discovering, validating and fixing software vulnerabilities a continuous, scalable capability that helps protect critical systems.

We’re excited about what we can build together and look forward to officially welcoming the AISLE team to Cohere.

# Canada’s AI Firm Cohere Tops CAD 35bn Valuation in Latest Fundraising

2 Nov 2026   3 min read

![Author Image](https://slator.com/assets/2026/05/Elias-Glenn-36x36.png)  [By Elias Glenn](https://slator.com/author/elias-glenn/)

![Presenter speaks onstage at Slator London beneath RWS and Cohere logos.](https://slator.com/assets/2026/11/velora-5731ac2566cdac73.png)

Canadian enterprise AI company Cohere on October 29, 2026, announced it had [completed the first closing in its Series E funding](https://cohere.com/blog/who-gets-to-build-the-frontier-for-ai), a round with a target of up to CAD 7bn. Germany’s Schwarz Group is leading the round, with participation from Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital, Inovia Capital, NVIDIA, Prosperity7 Ventures, and the Government of Canada.

Cohere said the round is the largest ever raised by a private Canadian company and values the company at CAD 35.7bn. The Canadian government [will invest](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/speeches/2026/10/29/prime-minister-carney-announces-landmark-investment-cohere-scale-secure) up to CAD 1.6bn in Cohere, Prime Minister Mark Carney said, and in return the company will keep its headquarters in Canada and invest CAD 1.7bn in Canadian computing infrastructure.

Cohere had previously raised approximately USD 1.57bn and said separately it is “advancing plans to invest more than C$4 billion in R&D and AI infrastructure [in Canada] and create over 1,500 jobs through 2031.”

![Partner spotlight](https://slator.com/assets/2026/04/Group-18-1.svg)

Partner spotlight

**What enterprise AI is missing**

Why AI-led content stalls in global markets, per 200 leaders

[Download the report](https://www.rws.com/about/content-unlocked/lp/)

![Partner spotlight](https://slator.com/assets/2026/04/Group-2.svg)

Partner spotlight

**Smartling Named a Leader**

The Forrester Wave™: Localization Services, Q3 2026

[Read the Report](https://bit.ly/4jt68QE)

Among frontier AI labs, Cohere holds a unique position in the language solutions and AI industry through its direct involvement in building Language Weaver Pro, an enterprise translation system [developed](https://slator.com/rws-cohere-build-trust-enterprise-translation/) with language solutions integrator (LSI) [RWS](https://slator.com/tag/rws/). The two companies continue to work together, releasing the [North Small Translate](https://slator.com/cohere-rws-ai-translation-model/) model on September 10, 2026. At SlatorCon London 2026, RWS and Cohere representatives [discussed](https://slator.com/rws-cohere-build-trust-enterprise-translation/) how the companies addressed translation quality, scale, security, and private deployment when developing Language Weaver Pro.

Proceeds from the new investment round will go toward the development of frontier and smaller models, Cohere’s North model-agnostic agentic AI platform, and cyber defense offerings. “We will use the funds to build something increasingly essential in AI: a frontier company outside the U.S. and China,” the company said.

Over the next 12 months, Cohere plans to complete its [combination with German company Aleph Alpha](https://slator.com/cohere-acquires-aleph-alpha/) and its acquisition of cybersecurity-focused company AISLE. Schwarz Group, an investor in Aleph Alpha, pledged USD 600m (approximately CAD 821m) in structured financing toward Cohere’s Series E when the merger was announced in April 2026.

### A Sovereign AI Alternative

Cohere is positioning itself as a frontier AI alternative to the dominant US and China ecosystems, offering sovereign AI to governments and regulated enterprises that want to run systems within their own environments. The company argues that reliance on a small number of providers leaves customers exposed to abrupt changes in access driven by commercial decisions, export restrictions, or geopolitical events. It links this strategy to the Sovereign Technology Alliance launched by Canada and Germany earlier in 2026.

> “We don’t have to accept a future of AI run by just a few, and we shouldn’t want one,” Cohere said in its latest funding announcement.

The Aleph Alpha deal aims to build a transatlantic sovereign AI business serving governments and regulated industries. The companies [signed a definitive agreement](https://aleph-alpha.com/en/news/cohere-agreement-transatlantic-sovereign-ai/) on September 16, 2026, with completion subject to final regulatory approvals. Cohere also plans to introduce Cohere Cyber for classified environments, release its next generation of models, and begin frontier-scale training with allied partners.

Cohere has signed a letter of intent to acquire AISLE, an AI cybersecurity company developing autonomous systems that discover and help remediate previously unknown software vulnerabilities, in a proposed transaction aimed at strengthening Cohere’s sovereign AI platform and cybersecurity capabilities

The proposed acquisition would bring together Cohere’s advanced AI models, agentic applications and secure deployment infrastructure with AISLE’s autonomous security technology, supporting organizations seeking to deploy AI across enterprise, government and highly regulated environments while maintaining control over their data and systems

The move would also expand Cohere’s presence in Europe, following its acquisition of Reliant AI and partnership with Aleph Alpha. Adding AISLE would further strengthen its capabilities in AI and cybersecurity for critical infrastructure, public-sector organizations and regulated industries

As enterprises and governments move AI applications from experimentation into production, security, data protection, governance and regulatory compliance are becoming increasingly important. Organizations also need to address software vulnerabilities and risks associated with autonomous AI systems while retaining the ability to deploy technology in private cloud, on-premises and fully air-gapped environments

Cohere said addressing these requirements calls for an integrated approach that combines advanced AI models, cybersecurity, governance and secure deployment rather than relying on model capabilities alone

Founded in 2025, AISLE has developed AI systems designed to identify, validate and help remediate previously unknown vulnerabilities in complex production software. Its technology combines foundation models with specialized security expertise, large-scale code analysis, rigorous validation and automated remediation

During its first year, AISLE identified more than 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities that were assigned Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers across more than 100 codebases. These included all 12 vulnerabilities in OpenSSL’s January security release and 18 of the 24 CVEs in curl’s latest release, according to the announcement. The vulnerabilities were independently reviewed by the relevant software maintainers

Cohere said combining AISLE’s autonomous security research with its frontier-model development and training could improve cybersecurity systems while creating opportunities to use complex, verifiable security tasks to assess and enhance future AI models

The proposed transaction would also support Cohere’s efforts to expand sovereign AI capabilities in Europe, where governments and enterprises are seeking advanced AI systems that meet strict requirements for security, privacy, regulatory compliance and data sovereignty

For customers, the combined capabilities are expected to strengthen threat detection across enterprise and public-sector deployments, improve governance, monitoring and observability for AI agents and autonomous workflows, and enhance protections for sensitive organizational data and mission-critical systems

The companies also aim to advance secure AI deployments across private cloud, on-premises and fully air-gapped environments, while developing cyber-resilient systems capable of identifying, prioritizing and responding to emerging threats

Cohere said the proposed acquisition reflects its view that organizations should retain control over their AI strategy, data, infrastructure and governance as AI becomes increasingly integrated into critical business and public-sector operations

By combining AISLE’s autonomous vulnerability research with Cohere’s AI models and sovereign AI platform, the companies aim to make software vulnerability discovery, validation and remediation more continuous and scalable, helping organizations strengthen the security of the systems on which their operations depend

# Cohere and Singapore's Centre for Strategic Infocomm Technologies Partner to Advance Secure, Enterprise-Grade AI for National Security Operations

![Cohere logo]( "Cohere logo")

## News provided by

05 Nov, 2026, 15:30 CST

## Share this article

Share this article

*The partnership strengthens Singapore's AI capabilities with secure, enterprise-grade AI designed for mission-critical operations*

SINGAPORE, Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cohere, a leading provider of sovereign AI for governments and regulated industries, today announced a strategic partnership with Singapore's Centre for Strategic Infocomm Technologies (CSIT) to advance the adoption and deployment of AI applications in highly secure environments, in support of Singapore's national security operations.

Through the partnership, CSIT will leverage Cohere's enterprise-grade AI models and agentic AI platform, North, to accelerate the deployment of AI applications within highly secure environments. The collaboration will support a range of operational use cases while meeting stringent requirements for security, governance, and reliability.

"Cohere is deeply committed to helping enterprises and governments build long-term sovereign AI capabilities," said Andrew Chang, Vice President of APAC, Cohere. "Our partnership with CSIT reflects how Cohere's AI solutions can meet the unique security, governance, and deployment requirements of public sector organizations while delivering the advanced AI capabilities needed for national security."

Following a successful pilot that demonstrated Cohere's ability to deploy and operate AI within secure on-premises environments while integrating seamlessly with existing systems and workflows, CSIT and Cohere are building on this foundation to explore a range of high-impact use cases. The collaboration includes building and evaluating potential applications including secure knowledge retrieval, automated analysis and report generation, and agentic workflows designed to streamline national security operations.

"As cyber threats grow in sophistication and threat actors use AI to amplify their attacks, CSIT is developing AI-enabled capabilities to strengthen Singapore's digital defence and secure our digital systems," said Alvin Huang, Chief, Data and AI at CSIT. "Cohere's enterprise-grade models and North platform provide a strong foundation for advancing AI adoption in secure networks, while maintaining the stringent security and governance standards such environments demand. CSIT looks forward to partnering with Cohere in shaping their platform to enable secure and effective use of AI."

As part of the partnership, CSIT will benefit from capabilities specifically designed for government, defense, and critical infrastructure organizations, including:

The announcement builds on Cohere's growing momentum across APAC, where the company works with leading organizations including Fujitsu, LG CNS, and public sector institutions such as Japan's Digital Agency to deploy secure, enterprise-grade AI systems.

Over the past year, Cohere has expanded its APAC customer base fivefold and continues to see strong growth across highly regulated industries, including financial services, manufacturing, energy, technology, and the public sector. To meet growing demand for secure, enterprise-grade AI solutions, the company plans to quadruple its regional presence by the end of 2027 through new investments, local partnerships, and additional offices across APAC.

**About Cohere**

Cohere, founded in 2019, is a leading provider of sovereign AI for regulated industries and governments that enables organizations to own, operate and govern their AI systems with greater control over their data, infrastructure, and deployment. Our all-in-one platform provides maximum security, privacy, and deployment flexibility across public and private clouds, on-premises environments, and fully air-gapped settings. Headquartered in Toronto, Cohere operates in San Francisco, London, New York, Berlin, Montreal, Ottawa, Singapore, Paris, Tokyo, United Arab Emirates, and Seoul, serving customers worldwide. For more information, visit [cohere.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4814610-1&h=3631502213&u=http%3A%2F%2Fcohere.com%2F&a=cohere.com).

**About CSIT**

The Centre for Strategic Infocomm Technologies builds advanced cybersecurity and secure digital solutions that safeguard Singapore's national security. CSIT conducts applied research in cybersecurity and develops AI and data exploitation tools in our self-built secure cloud environment. Our engineers' codes protect a nation, counter digital threats, and secure our most sensitive secrets. CSIT is an agency of the Ministry of Defence and a member of the Defence Technology Community. For more information, please visit [www.csit.gov.sg](http://www.csit.gov.sg)

Media Contact, Amanda Taggart, Vice President, Global Communications @ Cohere, [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#aededccbddddeecdc1c6cbdccb80cdc1c3)
