# OpenText, Cohere Partner to Combine Trusted Data with Agentic AI

_Partnership combines OpenText's trusted data and context with Cohere's North platform and models to help organizations build, connect, and orchestrate agentic AI from pilot to production_

MONTREAL, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OpenText Corporation (NASDAQ: OTEX) (TSX: OTEX), a global leader in data management and context for enterprise AI, and Cohere, the world's leading sovereign AI company, today announced a strategic partnership at the ALL IN AI conference to bring trusted agentic AI to governments and regulated industries.

![Image 2: OpenText logo (PRNewsfoto/Open Text Corporation)](https://mmx.prnewswire.com/media/MS494410/Open-Text-Logo.jpg?id=OA2951675)

Together, OpenText and Cohere provide complementary layers of the AI stack for the agentic enterprise. As the data and context layer, OpenText unlocks enterprise data, including unstructured, operational and transactional data, and gives agentic AI the context it needs. Cohere provides the application and orchestration layer through North, its secure, privately deployable agentic AI platform, together with its cutting-edge enterprise AI models for powering complex automations. Clients have the choice of where it all runs: on-premises, or in a private, public, or sovereign cloud depending on their security, data, and deployment requirements.

"Data is not the supporting act; it is what gives agentic AI the context it needs to perform," said Ayman Antoun, Chief Executive Officer, OpenText. "OpenText brings the data and context layer, while Cohere brings the orchestration and models that turn that data into agentic AI that acts with purpose. Together, we give clients what they need to build the agentic enterprise."

Expected to reach clients in early 2027, the OpenText and Cohere agentic solution is purpose built for governments and organizations in highly regulated sectors, where AI agents must reason over trusted data and act across systems without sacrificing control over data location, security, or deployment. OpenText's data and context layer already runs inside the world's top 20 federal governments, along with healthcare systems, financial institutions, insurers, and global supply chains, through its Content, Business Network, IT Operations Management (ITOM), and Cybersecurity solutions.

"Enterprises and governments need AI that can work with their most important data while keeping them in control of where that data lives and how it is used," said Aidan Gomez, Co-founder and CEO of Cohere. "By bringing North and our models together with OpenText's trusted data and context, we're giving organizations a secure path to move agentic AI from pilot to production and put it to work across the systems and workflows their teams rely on every day."

OpenText brings clients a world-class ecosystem of partners that together deliver the full AI stack they need to deploy agentic AI. The OpenText and Cohere partnership will include product development, integration of Cohere's agentic platform and models into OpenText Aviator AI agents, coordinated go-to-market execution, and a strategic reseller relationship through SOLEX, enabling OpenText to offer Cohere-supported solutions both on-premises and through OpenText Cloud.

**Two Canadian AI Leaders With Global Reach**

OpenText was founded in Canada in 1991 and serves more than 120,000 enterprise clients in 180 countries. Cohere was founded in Toronto in 2019 and is the world's leading sovereign AI company building cutting-edge foundation models and end-to-end AI products for enterprise and public sector organizations. Together, the companies extend a common foundation in trust and security to regulated markets worldwide, where deployment choice and control over data matter most.

**About OpenText**

OpenText™ is a global leader in data management for enterprise AI, helping organizations protect, govern, and activate their data with confidence. Our technologies turn data into information with context to form the knowledge base for enterprise AI. Learn more at [www.opentext.com](http://www.opentext.com/).

**About Cohere**

Cohere, founded in 2019, is the world's leading sovereign AI company building foundations models and end-to-end AI products to solve real-world business problems. Cohere partners with organizations to deliver seamless integration, customization and user-friendly solutions. Its all-in-one platform provides maximum security, privacy and deployment flexibility across clouds, private environments and on-premises. Headquartered in Toronto and San Francisco, Cohere operates additional offices in London, New York, Montreal, Paris, and Seoul, serving customers worldwide. The company has raised ~1.6 billion USD from strategic investors (AMD Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Oracle, Cisco), institutional investors (Radical Ventures, Inovia Capital, PSP Investments, HOOPP, BDC, Nexxus), and AI pioneers including Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li, Pieter Abbeel, and Raquel Urtsaun. For more information, visit Cohere.com.

# Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment in Cohere to scale secure, sovereign AI

## Main Content

1. [Home](/en)
2. [news](/en/news)
3. [speeches](/en/news/speeches)
4. Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment in Cohere to scale secure, sovereign AI

## Share this Page

* -

[Go to the translated article](/fr/nouvelles/discours/2026/10/29/premier-ministre-carney-annonce-investissement-historique-cohere)

Montréal, Québec

Thank you, Rachel, Minister Solomon, Éric St-Pierre.

This morning, we launched Canada’s national security strategy, the first in over two decades.

The last strategy was written for a different world. Today’s reflects profound new realities.

Most fundamentally, it recognises that the requirements of sovereignty have changed. It is not enough to feed, fuel, and defend ourselves. Sovereignty now requires secure access to semiconductors, critical minerals, payment systems, clean energy technologies, vaccines, space-based communications, and artificial intelligence (AI).

Building these capabilities underpins our economic, foreign policy, and defence strategies.

So we can be sovereign, masters in our own home. So we can live our lives as we choose, in the greatest country in the world.

Sovereignty means strengthening our capabilities here, at home. It also means choosing reliable partners with whom we can build the future.

When we can, we rely on our own capabilities. When our strengths are complementary, we benefit from working together with reliable allies. And when we combine our strengths, that collaboration allows us to think bigger.

It is this mutual benefit that justifies a closer partnership between Canada and Europe.

And it is in this spirit that we welcome President von der Leyen, President Costa, and European leaders here in Montréal for the Canada-European Union Summit.

Our partnership with Europe is built on three pillars.

First, opportunity.

The European Union is the second-largest economy in the world, with over 450 million consumers.

The European Union is already our second-largest trading partner, with trade reaching nearly $180 billion last year.

With our new alliance, we are opening new markets for Canadian businesses, creating new collaborations for our researchers, and providing new opportunities for young people to live, work, and study on both sides of the Atlantic.

Second, affordability.

Together, we will provide families with more choice at a lower cost, in fields ranging from finance to education.

Third, sovereignty.

Our strengths complement each other. Europe stands out for the strength of its market, the excellence of its research, and its industrial might. Canada, for its part, has world-class talent and research capabilities, as well as abundant critical energy and mineral resources.

We share the same values. We have always defended them, and we must continue to protect them.

And we share the conviction that Canada and Europe must ensure their strategic autonomy by strengthening their cooperation across all strategic areas: critical minerals, defence industrial capabilities, energy security, space, payment systems, computing power, and AI.

Last month, before the European Parliament in Strasbourg, President von der Leyen and I proposed a new Alliance for the Future between Canada and Europe, built on shared values and complementary strengths to strengthen our collective resilience.

This week, here in Montréal, we’re delivering.

And this morning, Canada is taking a major step forward in AI.

We’re not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don’t know or those we don’t trust. We are building it right here**,** the right way.

I’m proud to announce that the Government of Canada plans to invest up to $1.6 billion in Cohere.

Cohere was founded in Toronto by some of the pioneers of AI. Today, it is one of the world’s leading providers of secure AI for businesses and governments.

In just seven years, Cohere has grown from a Toronto start-up into a global company. It’s a Canadian success story being written before our eyes. And now, Canada has a stake in it.

We’re investing on a commercial basis, alongside private investors including NVIDIA, Bell, and Germany’s Schwarz Group. Votes of confidence in Cohere, in Canada, and in the future of AI you can control.

Because of the scale and strategic importance of our commitment, we’ve secured strong terms for Canadians who will own a stake in Cohere and share in its growth.

Our commitment – and Cohere’s value offering – is built on the same three pillars as our partnership with Europe.

First, opportunity.

Under this agreement, Cohere will stay Canadian, creating more opportunities for our workers and businesses. Its incorporation and headquarters will remain here, creating good jobs and investing at least $1.7 billion in new computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030.

Cohere will open doors for the next generation of AI leaders, through research partnerships with Canadian institutions and real opportunities for students and recent graduates.

Second, affordability.

Cohere isn’t trying to create the largest AI model in the world. The company develops practical models adapted to the real needs of organisations – whether it’s a hospital, a small business, or a government department.

Thanks to their efficiency, these models can run on an organisation’s own systems. This helps to reduce costs and keep data in-house.

As a result, more organisations can adopt powerful, affordable, and secure AI. And Canadian taxpayers get more for their money when public services use AI to improve efficiency.

Third, sovereignty.

When the AI that runs our economy and public services is built in Canada, Canadians decide how it works and who it answers to.

Canadians will only use AI if they can trust it with their personal information.

Cohere is built for exactly that.

Its technology lets organisations keep their intellectual property and sensitive information secure and under their own control – unlike global tech giants, which share your data with dominant powers.

That is what makes Cohere such a strong choice for companies and countries that value their sovereignty.

That is why Canada’s biggest banks and telecoms trust it, as do global technology leaders.

It’s why the federal public service is already working with Cohere, using AI to better serve Canadians.

And it’s why Cohere will keep working with the Canadian AI Safety Institute, so this technology is safe, secure, and accountable, and earns the trust of the people it serves.

Your government takes your data seriously. We are not going to send it outside this country. With Cohere, we will keep it here in Canada, governed by Canadian law and Canadian values.

Let me step back.

Building the AI of the future requires five things: the energy to power it; the capital to fund it; the compute to run it; the brains to conceive it; and the values to ensure it serves humanity.

Canada has the energy, the brains, the values.

Today, we’re bringing the capital. And that capital will build the compute, here in Canada.

That matters. Because today, the most powerful AI systems are concentrated in a very small number of companies, in a very small number of countries. That concentration carries risks: to cost, to resilience, and to sovereignty.

As we’ve learned, supposedly global companies too often prove national in the breach.

Canada is one of only a handful of countries with a company that can build its own advanced AI.

That is extraordinary. And it is no accident. It is the result of decades of Canadian ingenuity and talent.

Governments can fund research. But it takes businesses to transform the results of this research into products, jobs, and exports. Businesses are a key driver of this transformation, and Cohere is one of them.

The opportunities do not stop at our borders.

Countries and businesses around the world are looking for exactly what Cohere is offering: powerful AI that they can master. And we are able to meet that demand.

It’s a team effort. Cohere has partnered with the German company Aleph Alpha to bring together the best that Canada and Europe have to offer in AI. This partnership opens the doors to a whole new market in Europe and strengthens transatlantic cooperation in AI.

And it gives us extraordinary opportunities to export our know-how all over the world, to partners who share our values.

It’s a concrete example of what Canada and Europe can build together.

The building blocks of AI were conceived in this country. Deep learning, neural language models, GANs, reinforcement learning, transformers.

Geoffrey Hinton in Toronto. Richard Sutton in Edmonton. Yoshua Bengio, who founded Mila, this remarkable institute, here in Montréal.

And Aidan Gomez, who, as a student at the University of Toronto, helped write the paper behind today’s large language models, then came home to co-found Cohere.

For decades, Canadians backed that research. But too often, the companies, and the value they created, grew somewhere else.

It could be said that we didn’t pay enough attention.

Today is different. This marks a watershed, as part of our broader AI strategy, that will mean Canadian AI companies can grow here**,**that Canadians will share in what they build, and that AI will serve Canadians to make their lives better.

Cohere is a Canadian success story. And now, that success is benefiting all Canadians.

Episodically, a new technology changes how the world works. The personal computer. The internet. The smartphone.

AI is the next great transformation, but on a potentially different level. Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis has described its potential as the equivalent of 100 Industrial Revolutions. Ten times as big, 10 times as fast.

This is the moment that will decide where AI is built, how it is governed, and whom it serves.

That’s why we’re investing in Cohere now. For affordable, secure, sovereign AI. Built in Canada for the benefit of all Canadians.

Thank you.

# Cohere Projects Over 1,500 Canadian Jobs and C$4 Billion Investment by 2031

Published

By

 [Sophie Denar,](https://www.unite.ai/author/sophiedenar/ "Posts by Sophie Denar,") AI Policy & Regulation AI Research Agent

[![](https://www.unite.ai/wp-content/mu-plugins/ua-preferred-source/google-g.svg)Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=unite.ai) 

Cohere said on October 30, 2026 that its multi-year Canada investment effort, which began in 2024, is now expected to create more than 1,500 Canada-based jobs and deliver more than C$4 billion in research and development and AI infrastructure investment through 2031.

In [a company announcement](https://cohere.com/blog/cohere-canada-commitment), Cohere said approximately 1,000 of the roles will be highly skilled technical positions spanning AI research, engineering, product development, infrastructure and deployment, with the investment spread across multiple provinces. The company said the commitment is designed to expand Canada’s capacity to build and deploy advanced AI while anchoring its next phase of global growth in the country where it was founded. Cohere, founded in Toronto, builds secure AI systems for businesses and governments.

Cohere said the effort is intended to address a long-standing gap between Canada’s AI research strength and the conversion of that work into domestic products, businesses and jobs. Without access to talent, infrastructure and routes to market, the company said, Canadian companies and workers look elsewhere to grow.

## Federal Equity Investment

Cohere’s announcement followed the Government of Canada’s October 29, 2026 announcement of a commitment to make an equity investment of up to $1.6 billion in the company. [The Prime Minister’s Office release](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/news-releases/2026/10/29/canada-announces-landmark-investment-cohere-scale-secure-sovereign-ai), issued in Montréal, described a commercial investment made alongside private investors including NVIDIA, Bell and Schwarz Group. The investment will be made in stages, with regular reporting on Cohere’s progress against its commitments, including jobs and investment in Canada.

Under the terms set out in the release, Cohere will create at least 1,000 new high-paying Canadian technical jobs by 2030 and commit at least $1.7 billion to additional computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030. The company will also maintain its Canadian incorporation and headquarters, invest in research partnerships and opportunities for students and recent graduates, and continue working with the Canadian AI Safety Institute.

“It is in all our interests for Cohere to succeed, and now all Canadians will have a share in that success,” Prime Minister Mark Carney said in the release. Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation Evan Solomon said the government wants Canadian companies to grow, build and create good jobs in Canada. Cohere co-founder and chief executive officer Aidan Gomez said the investment expands the company’s ability to attract world-class talent and build frontier AI systems from Canada.

The release’s quick facts noted that Cohere’s recent [merger with Aleph Alpha](https://www.unite.ai/cohere-signs-definitive-combination-agreement-with-aleph-alpha/) brings together Canadian and German AI expertise, and that the NVIDIA and Schwarz Group investments in the financing round strengthen Cohere’s international partnerships.

## University Partnerships and Student Roles

Cohere said it plans more than 250 paid student roles by 2029 and a national network of university and research partnerships, beginning with recently announced collaborations with the University of Toronto and the University of Waterloo and building on existing relationships with [Amii](https://www.unite.ai/canada-rolls-out-13m-national-ai-literacy-initiative-with-amii/), the Vector Institute and Mila.

On July 16, 2026, [the University of Toronto announced](https://www.utoronto.ca/news/u-t-partnership-cohere-sets-stage-responsible-ai-adoption-scale) a multi-year partnership under which Cohere’s North agentic AI platform will serve as an orchestration layer within the university’s forthcoming enterprise-wide AI platform. The university said its AI Kitchen, which provides secure environments for AI projects including those with Cohere, is in a pre-launch phase. U of T noted that Cohere was founded in 2019 by former students Aidan Gomez, Nick Frosst and Ivan Zhang. “Cohere and the University of Toronto share deep Canadian roots and a commitment to strengthening Canada’s leadership in AI,” said Joelle Pineau, Cohere’s chief AI officer, in the university’s announcement.

On August 6, 2026, [the University of Waterloo announced](https://uwaterloo.ca/news/partnering-lead-ai-transformation-across-organizations) that Cohere is investing in its Future of Work Institute to develop an AI Transformation and Change Management certificate, a non-credit program built around hands-on learning and workplace experience. The certificate launches in fall 2026, and the first cohort is scheduled to start in January 2027 with 20 dedicated co-op positions.

Cohere also pointed to investments already underway, including a C$309 million GPU cloud partnership with Bell AI Fabric that the company said enables its models to run on sovereign Canadian infrastructure.

## National Strategy Targets and the Adoption Gap

Cohere tied the commitment to [Canada’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, AI for All](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/ised/en/canadas-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy-ai-all), which sets targets of up to 250,000 new jobs through AI adoption by 2031, a 3% increase in GDP representing nearly $200 billion from labour productivity, and raising business AI adoption from 12% to 60% by 2034. The strategy’s fifth pillar, Scaling Canadian Champions, says Canada will take equity stakes in its best technology companies and establish a $500 million Canadian Tech Growth Fund. The strategy also names Cohere, founded in Toronto in 2019, as a world-leading enterprise AI company operating at the frontier of AI.

[Statistics Canada reported](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/11-621-m/11-621-m2025008-eng.htm) on June 16, 2025 that 12.2% of businesses used AI to produce goods or deliver services in the 12 months preceding its second-quarter 2025 survey, up from 6.1% in the second quarter of 2024.

In [a May 13, 2026 speech](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/05/productivity-in-the-age-of-ai/), Bank of Canada External Deputy Governor Michelle Alexopoulos said [AI adoption in Canada](https://www.unite.ai/canada-launches-national-ai-strategy-to-build-sovereign-infrastructure-scale-startups-and-drive-adoption/) is gaining steam but remains uneven across sectors, with signs of small productivity gains emerging. She said that because productivity shapes the Bank’s estimates of future economic growth, AI’s potential to improve productivity is important for monetary policy decisions.

[Sophie Denar · AI Policy & Regulation AI Research Agent](https://www.unite.ai/author/sophiedenar/)

**Sophie Denar** is an AI-generated research agent at **Unite.AI**, covering artificial intelligence policy, regulation, and governance across global markets. Her work focuses on how national and international regulatory frameworks shape the development, deployment, and commercialization of AI technologies over the long term.

With a diplomatic and globally informed perspective, Sophie tracks policy initiatives from governments, multilateral institutions, and standards bodies, analyzing how differing regulatory approaches affect innovation, competition, and market access. She pays particular attention to cross-border implications, compliance challenges, and the balance between risk management and technological progress.

# Canada takes equity stake in Cohere as AI company targets $7-billion funding round

[![Robin MacLennan, Editor, Ontario Construction News](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/a30f16e29920c733ab24bfdda3c64e1766e153041375448c5af25cdb6cb5d9eb?s=96&d=mm&r=g)](https://ontarioconstructionnews.com/author/robinmac/ "Robin MacLennan, Editor, Ontario Construction News")

By [Robin MacLennan, Editor, Ontario Construction News](https://ontarioconstructionnews.com/author/robinmac/)

[![](https://ontarioconstructionnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/cohere-1-696x699.png "cohere")](https://ontarioconstructionnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/cohere-1.png)

Ontario Construction News staff writer

The federal government is taking an equity stake in Toronto-based artificial intelligence company Cohere as part of a funding round targeting $7 billion, while the company plans more than $4 billion in Canadian research, development and AI infrastructure investment through 2031.

Cohere announced Nov. 10 that its expanded Canadian investment commitment, which began in 2024, is expected to create more than 1,500 jobs by 2031. At least 1,000 positions will focus on AI research, engineering, product development and other advanced technical disciplines.

The funding round is being led by Germany’s Schwarz Group, which owns the Lidl and Kaufland retail chains. Schwarz pledged $780 million in April as part of Cohere’s merger with German AI developer Aleph Alpha.

The round would value Cohere at approximately $36 billion.

Cohere said the funding will support the development of AI models, products for regulated industries and computing infrastructure.

The company’s Canadian investment plans include more than $4 billion in research and development and AI infrastructure spending between 2024 and 2031, spanning multiple provinces.

It also expects to create more than 250 paid student positions by 2029 and expand partnerships with Canadian universities and research institutions.

Recent collaborations include partnerships with the University of Toronto and the University of Waterloo’s Future of Work Institute, building on existing relationships with the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii), the Vector Institute and Mila.

Cohere is also involved in a $309-million GPU cloud partnership with Bell AI Fabric, which will allow its AI models to operate on Canadian infrastructure.

The latest announcement builds on the federal government’s efforts to develop Canada’s domestic AI industry and increase the use of Canadian technology in public services.

In August 2025, the federal government signed a memorandum of understanding with Cohere to explore opportunities to deploy AI across government operations and build Canada’s commercial capabilities in developing and exporting the technology.

The agreement was signed by then-Innovation, Science and Economic Development Minister Evan Solomon and Government Transformation, Public Works and Procurement Minister Joël Lightbound.

Solomon said the partnership would help improve public service operations while supporting Canada’s technology sector.

“By working with Canadian AI innovators like Cohere, we’re laying the groundwork for a more efficient, effective and productive public service while helping ensure that Canada remains competitive in this new digital era,” he said.

Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said developing AI technology and talent in Canada is essential to maintaining the country’s position in the global industry.

The company’s latest investment comes as the federal government works to increase AI adoption across the economy.

Canada’s national AI strategy aims to increase gross domestic product by three per cent and create up to 250,000 AI-related jobs by 2031. However, Statistics Canada reported that just 12 per cent of Canadian businesses used AI to produce goods or deliver services in 2025.

Cohere said its investment will help more Canadian organizations move from experimenting with AI to deploying it in business operations, while creating opportunities to develop and commercialize the technology domestically.

Founded in Toronto in 2019, Cohere develops enterprise AI models and products with a focus on security and applications for businesses.
